Country brief: hubs, employers, pay and standing

In Sofia, and to a lesser degree Plovdiv and Varna, the open door for graduates is the IT, outsourcing and shared-service sector of international firms, which recruits in English; the sector counted 833 companies and 105,436 full-time employees in 2024.
Outside it, hiring runs largely through personal contacts and in Bulgarian.
Service and IT centres: direct application

Ranked first on size: the outsourcing and technology-services sector had 833 companies (412 in IT, 388 in business processes) and 105,436 full-time employees in 2024. Junior specialists earned a mean of about €1,517 a month gross in 2024, the lowest of the region’s surveyed countries.
For experienced hires, Rivermate says skilled technology and business-process professionals are quickly snapped up by foreign employers.
Summer internships at technology firms

Progress (Telerik’s owner) runs a paid internship in Sofia, July to September: a CV, a 90-minute HackerRank test, then an onsite interview of 75–90 minutes; it states that more than 75% of its technical interns have received job offers. An event page lists 13 internship places and says applications open on 20 April (year not stated).

TechnoLogica’s 2026 internship ran from 20 July to 30 September, with applications closing on 22 June, in software development and databases; strong performers may receive a permanent offer in Sofia, Burgas or Varna.
Industry academies: Telerik Academy and SoftUni

Telerik Academy says it partners with over 60 top technology companies in Bulgaria and that 68% of its graduates were employed within two months of finishing; its Upskill programmes last three months.

SoftUni says it has trained 17,000+ developers, that 97% of its programming alumni started a tech job, and that it runs train-to-hire bootcamps and can hire junior developers from its alumni pool. These are the schools’ own figures.
Career Show fairs

Career Show Bulgaria, an expo for qualified staff, runs in three cities in October 2026: Sofia on 5 October, Plovdiv on 8 October and Varna on 15 October; it advertises 200+ employers, 100+ of them in Sofia, and free registration.
Employment Agency and job portals

EURES says private portals (jobs.bg, karieri.bg, zaplata.bg, jobtiger.bg, rabota.bg) are a widespread way to look for work, alongside the Employment Agency’s 106 local job centres and company websites, especially in IT and business-process outsourcing.
The Employment Agency runs the e-Job Exchange, a monthly schedule of job exchanges and the Youth Guarantee scheme, and showed 9,659 vacancies in August 2026.
Personal contacts
Outside the international centres, introductions through people already inside the employer count for more than portals. This is our reading; no survey was found.
No graduate intake calendar was found for Bulgaria: the centres and portals hire throughout the year, and the fairs fall in October (Career Show 2026: Sofia 5, Plovdiv 8, Varna 15 October).
The Employment Agency publishes a monthly schedule of job exchanges; the October 2026 one was listed.

Summer internships have a spring window: Progress’s event page says applications open on 20 April and its internship runs July to September; TechnoLogica’s 2026 deadline was 22 June for a 20 July start.
Academy cohorts are short: Telerik Academy’s Upskill programmes run three months and its Sprint courses two weeks.

The Technical University of Sofia is the engineering school employers visit: its 20th Career Days, reported on 6 October 2026, drew more than 70 companies, including Melexis Bulgaria, and continued in Plovdiv and Sliven.

We read no employer page that names target universities in Bulgaria. The tech academies (Telerik Academy, SoftUni) recruit from the general public aged 18–66 and from students, and Telerik’s partners include Accenture, SAP, Experian, KPMG, Paysafe and Progress.
Technical University of Sofia Career Days, 20th edition: reported on 6 October 2026 with more than 70 companies and hundreds of students, then Plovdiv and Sliven on the following days.

Career Show Bulgaria: Sofia (Arena 8888) 5 October 2026, Plovdiv (International Fair Plovdiv) 8 October, Varna (Gallery Graphite) 15 October; free, with lectures, employer panels and a CV photo studio in Sofia.
The Employment Agency’s monthly job exchanges (трудови борси) and AIBEST’s industry events, such as the SEE Forward summit.

Business graduates enter mainly through the finance, accounting and HR service centres in Sofia, which recruit juniors in English. This is our reading of the sector’s make-up; the 388 business-process companies in 2024 are the evidence of its size.

A distinctive route: many junior developers enter through industry academies, above all Telerik Academy (over 60 partner companies) and SoftUni (train-to-hire bootcamps). One Telerik alumnus, an IT student who added practical skills there, now works as a software developer.
No national graduate season was found; hiring runs all year, with fairs and monthly job exchanges as peaks. This is our reading.
The routes found, centres, portals and academies, ask for skills and languages rather than a master’s. This is our reading; no employer page states a degree level.

After the first review employers often ask for translated and authenticated education certificates; the Employment Agency also wants education documents authenticated by the issuing country, and Bulgarian programmes need a legal Bulgarian translation.
NACID, the national academic recognition centre, handles foreign diplomas and publishes a list of regulated professions, which need recognition.
The routes that employ most juniors, the academies and the centres, are skills-based, and no page read ranks universities. This is our reading.
We found no apprenticeship or dual-study route to graduate jobs; the structured routes are academies and the Youth Guarantee. This is our reading.
We found no figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hiring in Bulgaria; the Employment Agency lists vacancies centrally but does not break them down. “Medium” is a placeholder reading.

A non-EU hire needs the employer to advertise the vacancy at the Employment Agency for at least 15 days, and non-EU staff may not exceed 20% of the workforce (35% in small and medium firms); EU Blue Card hires are exempt from the test and the cap. See Visas for the rules.
A photo is usual on Bulgarian CVs; no page read states the norm, and Career Show runs a CV photo studio at its Sofia fair. This is our reading.
EURES recommends the Europass CV format; it states no page limit, so two pages is our reading of what is usual.
Employers usually expect a brief cover letter with the CV.
After the first review employers often ask for more documents, including references from former employers.
Prepare translated and authenticated education certificates and proof of work experience; employers ask for them after the first review.
No page read says whether a salary expectation is asked in the application; Rivermate says offers should be market-related and mix base pay with benefits. Our reading is that pay is raised later.
Employers asking for references from former employers is the only check found; we found nothing on background checks. This is our reading.
Portals, fairs and academies take open applications, while outside the international centres introductions count. This is our reading.
Centres recruit in English and applications are online; Rivermate says onboarding takes one to two weeks, and up to four months when immigration is involved.
English in international centres; Bulgarian elsewhere, and employment contracts must be written in Bulgarian.

Progress’s internship in Sofia has three steps: a CV (a portfolio or repository link is highly recommended), a HackerRank assignment of about 90 minutes to be finished within five days of the invitation, and an onsite interview of 75–90 minutes with several Progress professionals, covering technical and behavioural questions.

We found no page describing the selection stages of the finance and business-process centres, nor the usual time from application to offer or dress norms; general practice there is an interview with a language check. This is our reading.
After the first review, employers often ask for more documents: translated and authenticated education certificates, proof of experience and references from former employers.

A written employment contract is mandatory and must be concluded before you start; it must be in Bulgarian. The employer notifies the National Revenue Agency within three days and gives you a copy, and you can start only after registration.

Probation can last up to six months, and during it a worker may be dismissed without prior notice; for fixed-term contracts under one year it cannot exceed one month. After probation the notice is one month for an indefinite contract and three months for a fixed-term one.

The standard week is five days and at most 40 hours. Rivermate says two-thirds of companies pay bonuses, though they are not mandatory. We did not establish whether graduates negotiate or how long employers give to decide.

The employer must run a labour-market test by advertising the vacancy at the Employment Agency for at least 15 days, unless the job is on the shortage-occupations list, and the Agency gives an opinion (fee €51.13) before the single permit is issued.

Non-EU staff may not exceed 20% of a firm’s average annual workforce (35% for small and medium firms). EU Blue Card hires are exempt from the test and the cap but need a contract of at least six months at 1.5 times the average gross wage, which the library puts at €2,166 gross a month in 2026.

Ask early: Rivermate says onboarding takes up to four months when immigration is involved. Which employers actually sponsor, and what they want to hear, was not established; the international centres are the likely ones. This is our reading.

Portals named by EURES: jobs.bg, karieri.bg, zaplata.bg, jobtiger.bg, rabota.bg; the Employment Agency’s site (az.government.bg) and the EURES job-mobility portal; company websites, especially in IT and business-process outsourcing.
Bulgarian EURES advisers give information in English, German, Spanish and French; registration at the Employment Agency’s local job centres is free.
Career Show Bulgaria (careershow.bg) for fairs, Telerik Academy and SoftUni for developer training, and AIBEST (aibest.org), the outsourcing industry association, for member companies and events.

Arriving without translated and authenticated education certificates: employers ask for them right after the first review, and Bulgarian programmes need a legal Bulgarian translation of foreign diplomas.
Starting work before the contract is written and registered: the contract must be concluded in writing before the first day, and the employee can start only after registration.
Assuming English is enough everywhere: the centres recruit in English, but contracts must be in Bulgarian and elsewhere the working language is Bulgarian.
Waiting for the autumn to look for a summer internship: Progress’s applications open on 20 April and TechnoLogica’s 2026 deadline was 22 June.
Skipping the cover letter: employers usually expect a brief one.

Finance, accounting and HR centres recruit in English, while contracts must be in Bulgarian and local employers work in Bulgarian. Rivermate notes that Bulgarian workers often speak German, French and Nordic languages, which the centres value. The level and the evidence asked for (certificate, interview) were not established.
Bank jobs, such as UniCredit Bulbank or First Investment Bank in Sofia, work in Bulgarian; English is the language of the international finance centres. We read no listing stating a level.

Progress’s internship asks for very good written and spoken English and tests it in the interview; no certificate or CEFR level is named. Telerik Academy and SoftUni train in programming and say their graduates are hired by technology companies.

Eurostat counted 90.0% of Bulgarian tertiary graduates aged 20–34 who finished within three years as in work in 2025 (EU 85.3%), with youth unemployment of 13.1%: graduates are in demand, but this is a national figure that says nothing about the quality of the first job.

Progress states that more than 75% of its technical interns have received job offers after the internship, depending on performance and business needs; it is the employer’s own figure for all its offices, not for Sofia alone.

Telerik Academy says 68% of its graduates were employed within two months of finishing, and SoftUni says 97% of its programming alumni started a tech job; both are the schools’ own figures with no stated method.

Register as a job-seeker at the employment agency within seven working days of graduating, and apply to the Migration Directorate at least 30 days before your student permit ends.

Single permit

The employer applies while you are abroad, after advertising the job for 15 days with the employment agency, and non-EU staff may be at most 20% of the workforce (35% in small firms). The permit is tied to that employer and job.
Researcher permit, and PhDs

Doctoral scholarships are free of income tax and social contributions.
Working holiday
Bulgaria has no working-holiday or youth-mobility agreement with any country; the only seasonal route is a permit for farm and tourism work of 90 days to 9 months.
Short stay
Bulgaria is fully in Schengen since 1 January 2025: days here count in the same 90 in any 180, with no work. A tourist or visa-free stay cannot be converted inside Bulgaria.
Schengen visa
Nothing to arrange in advance: you may stay up to 3 months freely, with no visa or work authorisation.
Apply for the D visa at the Bulgarian consulate where you live: €100.

Staying over 3 months, register within 3 months at the regional Migration Directorate, with ID, a work contract registered with the revenue agency (or your employer’s statement) and proof of housing. Students bring their enrolment certificate, European Health Insurance Card and a statement that they support themselves.
Register your address within 3 calendar days of entering. In private rented housing this needs the owner’s notarised declaration of accommodation and a copy of the title deed.
The paper long-stay certificate is issued the same day, for €3.58 (7 BGN).
The biometric residence card costs €20.45 (40 BGN), on top of the fee for the permit itself.

The Interior Ministry assigns a 10-digit personal number for foreigners (LNCh) with your first long-stay residence document; the personal number EGN is only for Bulgarians and permanent or long-term residents.
Before you have it, the National Revenue Agency can issue a service number for tax, banking or company paperwork.
Employees are enrolled in the public health fund (NHIF) through their pay: 8% of gross, 4.8% paid by the employer and 3.2% by you.
Students and others not working are covered by their European Health Insurance Card, which they show when registering.
Students, interns, funded researchers and family members need private health insurance from an authorised insurer, covering at least €30,000 (60,000 BGN) for emergency care and repatriation.

Legal residents have a right to a basic account, but banks (UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, UBB, Fibank) in practice want you in person with your personal number card, and may charge non-residents for identity checks.

Applying for or renewing a permit gets you a receipt with a filing number: it keeps you legal in Bulgaria and, on a renewal, lets you keep working for the same employer, but it is valid only inside Bulgaria.
If your D visa has expired and the card is not ready, do not travel to or through other Schengen countries; only a direct flight home is safe.
Apply for the permit at least 14 days before your D visa expires; later, the application is rejected and you are unlawfully present.
Register your address within three days of arriving; in a private rental you need the owner’s notarised declaration and title deed.
Foreign criminal records expire six months after issue and must be translated by translators authorised by the Bulgarian foreign ministry.
The application receipt is valid only inside Bulgaria: with an expired D visa, only a direct flight home is possible.
Since the euro, state fees are being re-set: the EU registration certificate is reported at €7 (paper) or €18 (card), and other fees still need re-reading.
A draft would raise the D visa fee from €100 to €120.
Whether the 20% foreign-staff cap applies to Blue Card hires in start-ups is not settled.
Banks still make it hard for non-residents to open an account.

Canada’s distinctive door is co-op: degrees that alternate study terms with paid work terms, so students graduate with a year or two of Canadian experience and often an offer from a former co-op employer. Employers ask for “Canadian experience”, and co-op is how students get it.

Since 1 January 2026 Ontario employers with 25 or more employees may not require Canadian experience in a public job posting, but professional licensing rules are exempt and a posting that does not ask for it still goes to the candidate who already has it.
Co-op work terms

Waterloo says more than 8,000 active employers recruit from its co-op pool and that over 24,000 full-time positions a year are posted on WaterlooWorks and filled by co-op students; co-op graduates earn more and land jobs that better match their field.

Hiring runs in three cycles per term, each with postings, interviews, student ranking of employers and a match date: for the winter 2027 term, cycle 1 matches on 9 October 2026, cycle 2 on 13 November and cycle 3 on 27 November, and direct offers start after the last match.
Campus recruiting for CPA training positions

Accounting firms and banks hire students for CPA training roles through regional campus recruitment frameworks. CPABC describes two seasons, with the fall as the main one (most activity August to October) and spring running March to June, and larger firms often hire about a year ahead.
Some firms follow the regional deadlines and others set their own, so each firm’s process has to be checked; the Big Four also cut staff and hired fewer graduates in 2023 and 2024.
Bank rotational and new-graduate programmes

The big banks run structured entry: RBC’s CPA Rotational Program lasts 30 months in internal audit and finance and recruits in the summer for a start in the autumn of the following year; Scotiabank’s CPA stream also lasts 30 months and starts in June.

RBC’s other graduate entries are a Capital Markets programme for undergraduate or master’s degree holders and a permanent Analyst programme; the pages read give no application dates, so postings have to be watched.
Federal public service student and graduate hiring

The Federal Student Work Experience Program (FSWEP) keeps an ongoing inventory open all year for more than 200 departments and agencies; managers pick matching applicants for a test or interview, and citizens and permanent residents get preference.

The door is narrowing: the federal public service fell from 357,965 employees in March 2025 to 345,282 in March 2026, applications fell nearly 30% to under 735,000 in 2025-26, and Budget 2025 aims to cut about 40,000 positions by April 2029, about half of recent cuts being casual, student or term roles.
Direct application through boards and employer sites

The Government of Canada Job Bank, TalentEgg (co-op, internship and entry-level roles), Eluta and Indeed are the boards university career offices name, with a warning that boards alone are not the most effective method and that company sites should be checked first. Experienced hires apply the same way.

Ontario postings from 1 January 2026 must state the pay or a range (no wider than $50,000, and not needed above $200,000), say whether AI screens applicants and whether a vacancy exists; an interviewed applicant must hear within 45 days whether a hiring decision has been made.
Networking and referrals
Informational interviews and referrals matter much as in the US, especially for newcomers without Canadian experience.
A career office says boards are not the most effective method on their own and advises asking people in your field which boards they use.
Youth unemployment (ages 15 to 24) was 12.9% in August 2026, against 14.3% a year earlier and an average of 10.8% in 2017–2019; the all-age rate was 6.4%.
Cuts are visible where graduates apply: the federal public service shed more than 12,600 jobs in a year, and PwC and Deloitte Canada cut staff in 2023 and 2024.
Co-op and campus cycles are set a term or a year ahead, so the hiring year that matters is the one before the start date, not the year of graduation.

The big banks hire graduates into rotational programmes: RBC runs a two-year leadership programme of four six-month rotations plus capital-markets and technology tracks; Scotiabank’s programmes include a CPA stream.
The Big Four recruit accounting students on campus for CPA training contracts, but PwC and Deloitte Canada cut staff in 2023 and 2024, and the firms hired fewer graduates.

A CPA Ontario programme such as RBC’s asks for a recognised degree of at least 120 credit hours with a minimum 70% average, the Knowledge Assessment or CPA qualifying courses, and registration with CPA Ontario before the start.

The federal route is FSWEP for students and, for bilingual posts, a second-language test late in the process; the Communications Security Establishment, one of the federal employers, takes only Canadian citizens.
Co-op is the door to software: Shopify takes 40% of its interns from Waterloo and likes to hire them full-time after their terms; the banks run technology new-graduate programmes too.

AI hiring runs through the three national institutes and their professors: more than 850 students from Vector-affiliated AI master’s programmes have been hired by Ontario firms, and Mila in Montreal and Amii in Edmonton place students with partner companies and banks.

The Communications Security Establishment runs student placements for full-time Canadian college and university students, in Ottawa or by telework; it asks to apply about eight months ahead, and the security clearance for students takes about six months.

Waterloo is the co-op reference: more than 8,000 active employers recruit from its pool, and Shopify takes 40% of its interns there. Western’s Ivey MSc reported an 85% offer rate for 2023/24 and a median base of C$75,000.
CPA recruitment in each region is organised by the schools and the provincial CPA body, so your school’s career office decides which firms you meet and when.

Employers host their own information and networking sessions, universities offer events through career services, and CPABC runs information sessions, webinars and career events every month. Waterloo employers can also host information sessions.

Co-op hiring has three cycles in each of three terms (fall, winter, spring); the CPA firms hire mainly in the fall, from August to October, and again in spring; the federal student inventory is open all year.

Bank and CPA entries accept a bachelor’s, a postgraduate diploma or a master’s: RBC Capital Markets takes undergraduate or master’s degree holders and Scotiabank’s CPA stream takes bachelor’s, diploma and master’s graduates. Ivey’s pre-experience master’s reported an 85% offer rate.

Foreign degrees are checked formally for immigration and for regulated occupations: an Educational Credential Assessment from an organisation such as WES, ICAS or the University of Toronto’s Comparative Education Service shows a foreign degree is equal to a Canadian one, but it does not give a licence.
Regulated occupations require licensing in the province where you work; the CPA route asks for a recognised degree of at least 120 credit hours and a 70% average.
Employers recruit where they have ties: Shopify takes 40% of its interns from Waterloo and Waterloo’s pool draws more than 8,000 employers. Outside those channels, the pages read do not rank schools.
Co-op plays the part of dual study: Waterloo posts over 24,000 positions a year for its co-op students, but co-op is a feature of particular universities and programmes rather than a national system.

The federal public service had 345,282 employees in March 2026, down from 357,965 a year earlier, and Ottawa–Gatineau has 194,000 people in public administration; Budget 2025 aims for about 40,000 fewer positions by April 2029.

An employer can use the Global Skills Strategy, which aims to process eligible, complete work permit applications within 2 weeks for a Global Talent Stream job, but the applicant must apply from outside Canada and the job must be on the eligible list. No photo, no date of birth; a short résumé in North American style. Job Bank says a photo is not the norm in Canada and can lower your chances, and advises leaving out age, marital status and religious or political views, and never giving your Social Insurance Number.
The government’s résumé guide limits the résumé to two pages, with the stress on recent experience and little space for jobs older than 15 years.
The Job Bank résumé guide does not address cover letters. In practice a short tailored letter is added when a posting invites one; no page read sets a rule.

Do not list references on the résumé; keep them on a separate sheet and give them only when asked. Choose former managers, and for newcomers international managers, professors or volunteer supervisors; ask permission first.

Applications do not ask for certified copies of diplomas; certified credential assessment is for immigration and licensing, and the CPA route checks credit hours and average through its own registration.
Ontario postings now state the pay or a range, so applicants are not asked to name a figure first; elsewhere Job Bank postings often show a range marked to be negotiated.

Employers generally need written, specific consent before a check. The common checks are criminal record (convictions in the RCMP database), education, employment and, rarely, credit; a Vulnerable Sector Check is for work with children, older people or people with disabilities.
Federal security roles go far beyond this: CSE says assessment and clearance can take 12 to 18 months, with a background check covering at least 10 years.
Formal channels work: Waterloo’s matching, the CPA campus rounds and the bank programmes are all applications, but a career office tells students that boards alone are not the most effective method.
Co-op and the post-graduation work permit come with a Canadian degree; hiring a new graduate from abroad needs a sponsored permit.
The faster Global Skills Strategy needs an online application made from outside Canada, and federal security roles require citizenship.

English, and French in Quebec and for many federal posts. Federal bilingual posts carry a three-letter language profile (reading, writing, speaking) at levels A, B or C, and Quebec firms with 25 to 49 employees must register with the French-language office from 1 June 2025.

Co-op matching is a short, scheduled sequence: employers post, students apply, interviews run over about two weeks, then both sides rank and the system matches them; interviews pause during reading week and holidays.

Ontario employers that interview must tell the applicant within 45 days whether a hiring decision has been made, and must say in the posting whether AI is used to screen applicants.

The probation length is set in the offer letter. In the federal public service it averages 12 months for positions of more than a year, and notice during probation depends on the employee class (for example 2 weeks or 1 month).

Ontario’s statutory notice of termination applies after 3 months of continuous employment: 1 week before the first anniversary, 2 weeks after 1 year, then one more week for each further year of service to a maximum of 8 weeks.
An offer is negotiable in the private sector; where Ontario postings now carry a range of no more than $50,000, the offer is expected to sit inside it.

Few pages name sponsoring employers. The employer-side tool is the Global Talent Stream of the Global Skills Strategy: for a job needing a labour-market assessment (LMIA) the employer provides a contract, an offer letter and a positive LMIA issued through the stream; for an exempt job the employer pays a compliance fee, and only top-level and degree-level jobs (TEER 0 or 1) qualify.
Ask early: the 2-week target runs from a complete application made from outside Canada, family members must apply at the same time, and biometrics are due within 2 weeks of the instruction letter.
Some federal employers cannot sponsor at all: CSE hires only Canadian citizens, and FSWEP gives preference to citizens and permanent residents.

Official: the Government of Canada Job Bank (jobbank.gc.ca), GC Jobs for the federal public service, and Ontario Public Service Careers for summer posts. Students also use TalentEgg, Eluta, Indeed, Workopolis Campus, Magnet and the university’s own board.

University career offices run the co-op and campus rounds (WaterlooWorks at Waterloo; CPABC publishes information sessions and webinars every month), and employer sites carry the programmes: RBC, Scotiabank, and the Communications Security Establishment’s student page.

Missing the fall window: CPABC says larger firms hire about a year ahead, with most activity from August to October, and each firm may set its own deadlines.
Leaving the federal route too late: CSE asks for an application about eight months before the start, and security clearance for students takes about six months.
Treating a degree assessment as a licence: an Educational Credential Assessment does not give a licence or a job, and regulated occupations need licensing in the province where you work.

The big-bank graduate pages read (RBC, Scotiabank) state no language level; Scotiabank’s careers site is offered in English, French and Spanish. Check the French requirement of Quebec roles separately.

The CPA route is run in the province’s own CPA body; the CPA Ontario conditions named by RBC (a recognised degree of 120 credit hours, a 70% average, qualifying courses) mention no language certificate.

Co-op software hiring runs in English at Waterloo; the pages read for Shopify and the banks’ technology programmes state no other language requirement.

Montréal’s AI sector (Mila, IVADO, Google and Meta research centres) sits in a province where businesses with 25 to 49 employees must register with the French-language office from 1 June 2025; the pages read state no level for AI roles.

In 2023 one worker in ten in the Zurich region — more than 103,400 people — worked in finance, generating CHF 32.8 billion; Zurich is by far Switzerland’s largest financial centre, with banks 43% and insurers 37% of the sector’s value added.
Switzerland is home to Google’s largest development centre outside the US, in Zurich.

Basel hosts the headquarters of Roche and Novartis in a life-sciences cluster of over 800 companies, the Bank for International Settlements, and about 30% of Swiss exports pass through it by river, air and rail.
The commodity trade body counts 215+ member companies, mainly around Lake Geneva, in Zug and in Ticino; the sector is about 2.3% of Swiss GDP.
Eurostat puts the GDP of the Bern metropolitan region at €78.6 billion in 2021.
Eurostat puts the GDP of the St. Gallen metropolitan region at €42.2 billion in 2021.
Eurostat puts the GDP of the Lucerne metropolitan region at €30.7 billion in 2021.

The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Zurich 10th in the world (up 1 place) and second in Western Europe after London, Geneva 12th (up 6) and third, and Lugano 21st (up 4) and fifth; in the sector tables Zurich is 6th for banking and for investment management and 4th for professional services, Lugano 8th for banking and Geneva 11th.

Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the value of Zurich’s start-up ecosystem at $44 billion (Europe’s average $14.3 billion), with $2.4 billion of seed and Series A funding in H2 2023–2025 and $7 billion of exits in 2021–2025.

In 2024 the median gross monthly wage of a full-time post in Switzerland was CHF 7,024: CHF 7,502 in the Zurich region and CHF 5,708 in Ticino.

In 2024 the median gross monthly wage of a full-time post was CHF 7,156 in north-western Switzerland, CHF 7,092 in central Switzerland, CHF 6,998 in the Lake Geneva region, CHF 6,964 in Espace Mittelland and CHF 6,623 in eastern Switzerland, against CHF 7,024 nationally.

In 2024 employees with a university degree in a full-time post earned a gross monthly wage of CHF 10,533 in Switzerland, those with a university of applied sciences degree CHF 9,288 and those with a federal vocational certificate CHF 6,390.

Of Switzerland’s seven metropolitan regions in Eurostat’s tables, Zurich has the largest GDP (€140.8 billion in 2021) and population (1,579,967 in 2023), followed on GDP by Bern (€78.6 billion), Basel (€64.9 billion), Lausanne (€58.3 billion), Geneva (€52.2 billion), St. Gallen (€42.2 billion) and Lucerne (€30.7 billion).

In 2022 employees under 30 in Swiss firms with 10 or more staff (public administration excluded) earned a mean of €70,488 gross a year (converted to euro by Eurostat), and those under 30 working as professionals €83,890, against €95,698 for all ages.

In 2025 the employment rate of Swiss residents aged 20 to 34 with a tertiary degree was 90.2% (90.1% for those who finished within the last five years); unemployment was 4.9% overall and 8.8% for the 15-to-24s, and GDP was €925.9 billion.
Roche says it was founded in Basel in 1896 and is today a leading provider of medicines and diagnostics in over 100 countries.

The canton of Zug had 131,705 jobs in 20,321 businesses in 2023, 47,525 of them in the city of Zug: 14,693 in wholesale trade, 7,781 in head-office management and consultancy, 7,093 in IT services, 4,946 in financial services and 4,710 in activities auxiliary to finance and insurance.

The canton of Zug’s largest private employers in 2024 included Roche Diagnostics International (2,833 employees in the canton), Siemens (2,121), AMAG (1,447), Glencore (1,175), Partners Group (569) and the Zuger Kantonalbank (560).

The Federal Statistical Office’s provisional figures for 2022 give the canton of Zug a GDP of CHF 25,176 million, or CHF 192,958 per inhabitant against CHF 90,131 for Switzerland and CHF 104,620 for the canton of Zürich.

At 31 December 2024 the City of Lugano counted 68,507 inhabitants and 17,579 registered businesses, of which 3,459 in finance, 2,321 in insurance, administrative and legal services, 1,627 in wholesale trade and 873 in information technology and telecommunications.

Swiss firms hire juniors they have already tried: interns from Swiss universities, often on six-month placements during the master’s, and graduates of their own trainee programmes. The banks recruit where they hold their own events, above all at St. Gallen, ETH and Zurich.
From abroad, without a Swiss university or an EU passport, the door is mostly closed.
The market has cooled for new graduates: in the 2025 federal survey 44.1% of master’s graduates of the class of 2024 said they had trouble finding suitable work, against 30% for the class of 2022.
Internship during the master’s
Banks, insurers and consultancies take six-month interns all year and pay well; 95% of St. Gallen master’s graduates had more than six months of practical experience.

In the federal survey, lack of experience is the main reason graduates give for not finding suitable work: about two-thirds of master’s graduates and almost three-quarters of university-of-applied-sciences bachelor’s graduates.
Graduate and trainee programmes
Large employers run rotation programmes for recent graduates: UBS’s graduate talent programmes ask for a degree from the last 18 months and, for Swiss degrees, a grade average of at least 4.5.

Roche’s Operations Rotational Development Program is a 2-year trainee programme in Basel/Kaiseraugst and Penzberg for master’s graduates in science or engineering who finished less than 2 years ago; its page gave the next application period as starting on 1 March 2026.
Campus recruiting
St. Gallen says 372 companies recruit on its campus each year and 86% of its master’s graduates hold a permanent job by graduation.

In 2025, 42 companies took part in the HSG Career Days, where 1,224 students sent 5,956 applications; the Banking Days drew 34 banking, investment and private-equity firms and 22,450 student applications. Outstanding HSG students can take part.
Direct application through job boards
The main boards are jobs.ch for German-speaking Switzerland and jobup.ch for the French-speaking region; talendo.ch is the board for students and recent graduates, with over 1,000 employers listed.
A formal file of CV, cover letter and certificates is expected, and a process takes two weeks to a month.
Public administration internships

The Federal Office of Justice takes master’s graduates in law (degree less than 1 year old) for internships of usually 5 to 6 months at 100%, advertised on the federal job portal (Stellenportal Bund).
Apprenticeship (Lehre)

Apprenticeship is the mainstream route for school leavers: in June 2026, 63% of young people were considering basic vocational training, about 74,000 positions were offered and 68% were already filled. It is not a way in for a graduate.

Unemployment a year after graduating rose sharply in the latest federal survey: from 3.9% to 6.4% for university master’s graduates and from 3.4% to 4.9% for bachelor’s graduates of universities of applied sciences. When non-EU hiring needs proof that no Swiss or EU candidate is available, a downturn closes that door first.

The biggest rises were in economics and business (master’s: 3.5% to 8.5%, classes of 2022 to 2024) and in engineering (2.1% to 4.8%). In the second quarter of 2026 Adecco counted job postings 2.4% below the previous quarter and, over the year, down 13% for commercial profiles and 10% for economic ones, while graduate IT postings rose 6%.

Swiss banking recruits through school-specific fairs such as HSG Banking Days; UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank, Raiffeisen and Swiss Re are among the partners. Private and cantonal banks want the local language of the region.
The Big Four recruit economics and business graduates into audit with a path to the Swiss certified accountant qualification, and run traineeships with St. Gallen.

Swiss multinationals run rotational programmes for recent master’s graduates: ABB’s Global Early Talent Program starts with an induction in Zurich and includes six months abroad; Roche and Novartis run their own.
Google’s Zurich office, about 5,000 people and its largest engineering site outside the US, sits next to ETH, and staff move between the two; ETH and EPFL are the main feeders for software roles.
IT is the part of the graduate market that grew: Adecco counts graduate IT postings up 6% in the year to the second quarter of 2026, while science, commercial and economic profiles fell.
AI and quantitative hiring run through ETH Zurich and EPFL: their labs, doctoral students and spin-offs, and the research centres of large tech firms in Zurich.
The federal administration offers internships to recent graduates, for example 5 to 6 months at the Federal Office of Justice for law master’s graduates, advertised on the federal job portal.
St. Gallen (HSG) is the gate to Swiss banking and consulting, ETH and EPFL to technical and quantitative roles; Zurich, Basel, Bern and Lausanne feed their regions.
HSG’s Banking Days are a flagship finance event open to outstanding HSG students who apply to attend; 22,450 student applications went to 34 firms in 2025.
Sector fairs run by the universities: HSG Career Days and Banking Days, and the company forums at ETH and EPFL.

The 2025 HSG Career Days covered seven sectors (consulting, law, industry, luxury goods, consumer goods, technology, insurance) with 42 companies; talendo.ch lists career fairs and networking events across Switzerland.

Swiss banks take six-month interns continuously, starting in January, April, July or October, with applications 3 to 5 months before the start. Programmes can have a fixed window: Roche’s page gave 1 March 2026 as the start of its application period.

The master’s is the usual entry for the programmes read: Roche asks for a master’s in science or engineering, and the federal survey reports on master’s graduates. At St. Gallen 95% of master’s graduates had more than six months of practical experience.
Recognition applies to regulated professions: the federal portal anerkennung.swiss shows, by occupation, whether a foreign qualification must be recognised and which body is responsible.
For other jobs no recognition procedure applies and the employer judges the degree.
St. Gallen is the gate to banking and consulting: 372 companies recruit on its campus each year, and its flagship Banking Days are open to outstanding HSG students who apply to attend.

Apprenticeship is the mainstream route into work: in June 2026, 63% of young people were considering basic vocational training and about 74,000 positions were offered, 68% of them already filled. Graduates do not use it, but employers are used to training their own staff.

The public sector is a smaller door for graduates than banks, pharma and multinationals in the pages read: the Federal Office of Justice takes law master’s graduates for internships of 5 to 6 months, advertised on the federal job portal.

Non-EU/EFTA nationals can work in Switzerland only if highly qualified, and the employer must show that no suitable candidate is available in Switzerland or the EU/EFTA. The Federal Council left the 2026 quota for third-country workers at 8,500 (4,500 residence permits and 4,000 short-stay permits); employers used 74% of the 2024 quota. See Visas for the rules.
Optional: include a professional passport-sized photo if the job advert asks for one. Employers may also ask for age, gender or marital status, though answering is not required.
Aim for one A4 page, short and concise, with bullet points.
Keep the cover letter to one page, usually four concise paragraphs, typed unless the company asks for a handwritten one, in the language of the job advert (German, French, Italian or English).

The guide advises listing references from previous employers. A new employer may contact a former one only with the applicant’s consent, which has to be explicit, and applicants may limit it to named people or firms.
Companies typically request a CV, a cover letter and educational certificates; the guide advises adding training certificates. Posted documents are usually returned.
Avoid raising salary and benefits at early interview stages; the interviewer may bring them up, and they are usually settled in later stages.

Reference checks are routine: in a survey of more than 500 HR managers 60% said they also gather personal information about applicants informally, which the press called a breach of data protection law. The lawful route is a reference with the applicant’s consent.
Formal applications with a complete file work; at the banks, being met at a school event first helps.
Internships are in practice open to Swiss and EU/EFTA citizens and to non-EU students enrolled at a Swiss university doing a required internship.
Overseas applicants may first face a phone or video interview.

In nine years of ads to early 2023, 87% mentioned German (counting ads written in German), 32% English, 23% French and 4% Italian; more than a third named two or more languages, most often German with English or German with French.
English is enough in global banking, consulting and tech teams.

Expect a formal interview of 45 to 60 minutes with your prospective boss present, possibly a second or third round, and conservative business dress; overseas applicants may first face a phone or video interview. The process can take two weeks to a month, and a thank-you message is advised.
At HSG’s Banking Days companies choose modules such as presentations, interviews, case studies and company dinners, so a first selection happens at the event.

Rotation programmes add stages: Roche’s Operations Rotational Development Program is a 2-year rotation across functional areas of Pharma Technical Operations, and UBS’s graduate programmes are rotational too. The pages read give no stage list for either.

Probation is usually 1 month and can be extended to a maximum of 3 months by written agreement, with 7 days’ notice on either side. After it, notice is 1 month in the first year of service, 2 months in years 2 to 9 and 3 months after that, each to the end of a month (Art. 335c CO).

A 13th month salary is not required by law; it exists only where the contract, a collective agreement or the personnel rules provide for it. In 2024, 75.9% of employees received one, so check the contract.
Salary is usually settled in later interview stages rather than in the application; a job offer should come with a thorough employment contract, and a probation period must be agreed in writing.

Third-country nationals are admitted only if highly qualified, usually with a higher-education degree and several years of experience, and the employer must show that no suitable candidate is available in Switzerland or the EU/EFTA, with pay and conditions matching regional and sector norms.
Quotas cap how many can be admitted: 8,500 qualified third-country workers in 2026 (4,500 B and 4,000 L permits), of which employers used 74% in 2024 and about 52% by the end of September 2025.

What an employer wants to hear is that you already hold the right to work, or the exact basis on which you will: say it in the first message, because the test and the quota are the employer’s paperwork and cost time.

Boards: jobs.ch (German, French and English versions) for German-speaking Switzerland, jobup.ch for the French-speaking region, and talendo.ch for students and graduates, which also lists career fairs and networking events.
University services: HSG Career & Corporate Services (Career Days, Banking Days) for St. Gallen; the federal job portal Stellenportal Bund for federal internships.
Programmes to look up: UBS graduate talent programmes, Roche’s Operations Rotational Development Program, ABB’s Global Early Talent Program and Deloitte’s St. Gallen traineeship.
Applying from abroad without a right to work: the third-country test and quota make employers cautious, and internships in practice go to Swiss, EU/EFTA citizens or students at a Swiss university.

Arriving at the end of the master’s without practical experience: two-thirds of master’s graduates who struggled to find suitable work named insufficient experience, and at St. Gallen 95% had more than six months.
Writing in the wrong language or a long CV: write in the language of the advert, one A4 page for the CV, one page for the letter.
Treating the 13th month salary as automatic: it is not required by law, so confirm it in the contract.
In French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino, 45% of ads for business and social-science graduate roles ask for German; in the ads as a whole more than a third name two or more languages.
Private and cantonal banks want the local language of the region; global banking teams work in English. The study of ads gives German with English or French as the common pairs.

English is the second most named language in Swiss job ads (32%) after German (87%); in French-speaking Switzerland 49% of ads for technical specialists ask for German. The pages read give no tech-only split.
AI roles sit in ETH and EPFL labs and in the research centres of large tech firms in Zurich; no language level is stated on the pages read.

A year after graduating, unemployment was 6.4% for university master’s graduates (3.9% in 2023) and 4.9% for bachelor’s graduates of universities of applied sciences (3.4% in 2023); 0.7% for teacher-training graduates.

The share saying they had trouble finding suitable work rose from 30% to 44.1% for master’s graduates and from 24.2% to 36.9% for bachelor’s graduates of universities of applied sciences (classes of 2022 to 2024); in economics and business it was 43.9% and in engineering and IT 39.6% (university of applied sciences).
The state of the economy was named as a reason by 42.5% of master’s graduates in 2025, up from 23.8% in 2023.

EU and EFTA citizens work in Switzerland under the free-movement agreement, with no labour-market test or quota: a contract of up to 364 days gives an L permit, a longer or open-ended one a B permit valid five years.
Register at the commune within 14 days of arriving and before your first day of work; the receipt lets you start. Up to 90 days of work a year need only an online notice by the employer.
Take out Swiss basic health insurance within three months; it is charged back to your arrival. A student who does not work can be exempted with the European Health Insurance Card.
Student visa (D) and B permit
Apply for the D visa at the Swiss embassy three to four months before term, with admission, a study plan and a written undertaking to leave when you finish; the canton decides.
No paid work in the first six months; after that, 15 hours a week in term with cantonal approval, full time in holidays.
Switzerland does not follow the EU student-mobility rules: a student permit from an EU country gives no right to study here, even on an exchange.
Funds in a Swiss bank (by canton)
CHF 21,000 a year in Zurich; CHF 24,000 in Vaud, Geneva, Basel and St. Gallen
Fees
CHF 90 visa, CHF 95 entry approval, CHF 142 to 182 permit
The student health exemption ends the moment you take any paid work, even a few hours as an assistant: then Swiss insurance at the full premium is compulsory.
Internships
Up to 90 days a year the employer only notifies the job online; from 91 days to a year you register at the commune and get an L permit.
Compulsory internship of a degree

Only an internship your degree, Swiss or foreign, requires, up to half the length of the course: the company applies to the cantonal labour office with the university’s certificate. Internships after graduating are not allowed, except under the young-professionals agreements or within the job-search months after a Swiss degree.
Six months to look for work after a Swiss degree
After a Swiss degree you may stay six months to find a job; the employer must then show the hire is of preponderant scientific or economic interest to skip the priority for residents.
The hire still needs a place in the annual quotas: a bill to exempt Swiss graduates was shelved.
Funds for the six months
CHF 10,500 in Zurich, CHF 12,000 in Vaud, Geneva and Basel
Specialist or manager permit (B or L)

Only managers, specialists with a university degree and highly experienced professionals qualify; ordinary jobs are closed to non-EU citizens. The employer must show no suitable candidate was found in Switzerland or the EU/EFTA, and pay the local and sector rate.
The canton and then the federal migration office approve; a quota place is needed: 4,500 B and 4,000 L permits in 2026, with a separate 3,500 for UK citizens.
CHF 322 to 329 in all
PhD and research posts
Swiss PhD students and postdocs are salaried staff; the university’s HR files the permit, and academic research enjoys easier admission, without the residents’ priority.
As employees they must join Swiss health insurance at the full premium.
Typical PhD salary
CHF 48,000 to 55,000 a year
Young professionals (stagiaires)

There is no working-holiday visa. Instead, citizens of 14 countries, the UK and the US among them, aged 18 to 35 with a degree or vocational qualification, can work full time in their own field for up to 18 months, outside the quotas and with no residents’ priority.
Short stay
Visits up to 90 days in any 180; any paid work, even for a day, needs prior cantonal approval for non-EU citizens.
Settlement (C permit)

Normally after ten years with a B permit, or five with good integration (B1 spoken, A1 written in the local language). Study years count only if followed by at least two years on an ordinary B permit.
EU and EFTA citizens usually get the permanent C permit after five years.

Line up housing that lets you register within 14 days: towns refuse registration on an Airbnb or hotel booking, and vacancy rates are 0.11% in Zurich and 0.31% in Geneva, so many newcomers book a serviced apartment first.
Once the canton approves, collect the D visa (90 CHF) before you travel; the permit fees in Switzerland are CHF 137 to 144.

Register with the residents’ office (Einwohnerkontrolle, contrôle des habitants) within 14 days of arriving and before your first day of work, with passport, lease or the main tenant’s accommodation statement, work contract or enrolment, 2 photos and civil-status papers. Working before registering counts as undeclared work.
The registration receipt (Meldebestätigung) lets you work and start other formalities while the biometric permit card is made, in 3 to 8 weeks.
With a work contract of a year or more you get a B permit valid 5 years.
Your 13-digit social insurance number (AHV/AVS, starting 756) is assigned through your employer’s compensation fund, or through the residents’ office for students and people not working.
Without a C permit, tax is withheld from your pay at source; earning CHF 120,000 a year or more, you must also file an ordinary tax return every year.

Take out basic health insurance within 3 months of taking up residence: it is backdated to day one, and if you miss the deadline the canton assigns you an insurer, with a late-payment surcharge. Premiums average CHF 393.30 a month in 2026, with a CHF 300 deductible and 10% co-payment up to CHF 700 a year.
Students can be exempted by showing a valid European Health Insurance Card and filing the cantonal exemption form within the 3 months; any paid work in Switzerland ends the exemption.
Students can be exempted with an equivalent private student policy (about CHF 38 to 115 a month) certified by the canton; any paid work in Switzerland ends the exemption.
PostFinance must open a basic Swiss franc account for anyone resident in Switzerland; private banks may refuse until you hold the permit card, and app banks (Neon, Yuh) accept only the card itself.

The registration receipt is not a travel document: if your D visa has expired before the card arrives, ask the cantonal migration office for a return visa (90 CHF), granted only for urgent reasons, before you leave.
Starting work before registering at the commune counts as undeclared work.
Miss the three-month health-insurance deadline and the canton assigns you an insurer at the standard model, with a late surcharge.
Communes refuse registration on an Airbnb or hotel booking; a serviced apartment booked before you arrive is the usual way out.
The commune’s receipt is not a travel document: leaving after your D visa expires and before the card arrives needs a return visa (CHF 90).
A posting notice filed even one day short of eight full days before work starts is treated as undeclared work, with fines and possible bans.
With a B, L or G permit, tax is withheld from your pay; above CHF 120,000 a year you must file a full return every year.
The new Switzerland–EU package (Bilaterals III), signed on 2 March 2026, still has to be ratified and may change free movement.
Switzerland may rejoin Erasmus+ in 2027; until then exchanges run through the Swiss SEMP programme.
Cantons differ on accepting temporary housing and sublets for registration.
What counts as “preponderant economic interest” for hiring a non-EU graduate of a Swiss university varies by canton.
Cantons differ on which foreign private policies they accept for the students’ health exemption.

Autumn and spring campus seasons

Autumn recruitment is the main drive: roughly September to November or December, when most graduate roles are advertised and filled. Tech firms open an early batch (tíqiánpī) in June or July, and the peak for large tech, consumer-goods, pharma and Big Four employers runs from August to October.
Most offers go out in November and December, with a supplementary round (bǔlù) in December alongside the first spring openings. Spring recruitment, usually March to April, fills what is left.
Huawei shows the rhythm: its graduate drive for the class of 2026 was announced on 15 August 2025, and its internship drive for the class of 2027 on 15 March 2026.
Whether a candidate counts as a fresh graduate (yīngjièshēng) is decided by the employer, and returnees generally hold no tripartite agreement (sānfāng xiéyì) with a school.

Komerční banka says one can be mentored there through an internship or a part-time job while studying.
Trainee programmes
Komerční banka’s Trainee program is for university students in the 4th or 5th year, recruits every spring, and lets participants start at the bank straight afterwards; the 2026 intake was full.
Škoda Auto runs a one-year Trainee Program for university graduates with Business, Tech and IT tracks that rotate through departments of the carmaker.
University job fairs and career days
VŠE’s ŠANCE fair is held twice a year, usually in April and October, with more than 100 companies including banks, consultancies and IT firms; the next one is on 20–22 October 2026.

The Career Days of CTU’s electrical and mechanical engineering faculties on 31 March and 1 April 2026 brought nearly 90 employers, among them Škoda Auto, ČEZ, Siemens and Valeo, to about 6,000 students.
Direct application through job portals
EURES names jobs.cz and profesia.cz among the private portals, alongside the Labour Office database, and says the overwhelming majority of employers require Czech.
Recruitment agencies
EURES says agencies must hold a licence listed on the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs portal and may not charge job-seekers; Randstad is the general partner of Charles University’s Career Day.
Public-sector selection procedures
Civil-service posts are filled through a selection procedure (výběrové řízení) that must be published in the civil-service information system ISoSS (portal.isoss.cz).
Komerční banka launches its trainee recruitment every spring; the 2026 programme was already full and the page pointed to May 2026 for the next round.
Internships follow the academic year: Red Hat’s Brno listings give expected starts of 1 February or 1 July, and JetBrains opens applications twice a year.
Fairs fall in spring and autumn: Charles University’s Career Day and CTU’s Career Days ran in March and April 2026, and VŠE’s ŠANCE is held in April and October.

Czech Technical University (CTU) is where the engineering employers meet students: its electrical and mechanical faculties’ Career Days drew nearly 90 firms, including Škoda Auto, ČEZ, Siemens, Valeo and Rohde & Schwarz.
The Prague University of Economics and Business (VŠE) runs ŠANCE, where more than 100 employers including banks, consultancies and IT firms meet its students and graduates.
Charles University’s Career Centre offers counselling, job and internship listings and an annual Career Day; we found no ranking of schools by employers.
Job Fair ŠANCE at the Prague University of Economics and Business, 20–22 October 2026 (10:00 to 16:30, Tuesday to Thursday).
Career Day at Charles University: in person in Prague 1 and online on 19 March 2026, free for its students and graduates.
Career Days of the Faculties of Electrical and Mechanical Engineering at CTU: 31 March and 1 April 2026, 10:00 to 16:00.

Prague and Brno’s service centres hire business graduates into finance and accounting operations, with German-language finance teams paying a premium; the Big Four and Czech banks recruit students through internships.
Škoda Auto’s Business Trainee track is for graduates of economics or business-focused universities.
Komerční banka’s Trainee program takes students in the 4th or 5th year and recruits every spring; the bank lists internships and part-time roles for students and graduates.

Prague is the main development and research centre of Gen Digital, the company formed from Avast and Norton, and Czech Technical University supplies most of its engineers; the merger also brought lay-offs in overlapping roles.
Red Hat’s Brno office takes paid student interns in software work (the listing read asks for Python or Go) for 12 to 24 months; JetBrains hires paid interns for 3–6 months.
Civil-service posts are announced as selection procedures in the ISoSS information system; the Ministry of Interior page read dates from 2015, so check current rules on the portal.
Trainee recruitment is in spring at Komerční banka, internships start in February or July, and fairs fall in spring and autumn; there is no single national season.
Komerční banka’s trainee programme is aimed at students in the 4th or 5th year (the master’s years), and Red Hat takes bachelor’s students from the 3rd year. This is our reading of a mixed picture.

EURES says only regulated professions need official recognition (nostrification) of a foreign qualification; the recognition itself is done by a Czech public university, or by the Ministry of Education when no comparable programme exists, and the pages read do not say employers in other fields ask for it.

Škoda Auto splits its trainee tracks by type of university (economics for Business, technical for Tech), and the employers at CTU’s and VŠE’s fairs go to those schools; the tech firms read ask for skills and a GitHub link rather than a named school.
We found no formal dual-study degrees, but part-time student internships are routine: Red Hat’s run alongside study for up to 24 months, and Komerční banka offers part-time roles for students.
Civil-service posts are filled through selection procedures published in ISoSS; we did not find a figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hires, so this is our reading.

A non-EU hire needs an Employee Card or an EU Blue Card; since 1 July 2024 the employer no longer runs a waiting-period vacancy test but must enter the post in the Labour Office’s central register. The large international centres and tech firms are the employers equipped to file it. See Visas for the rules.
A photo is the norm on Czech CVs; choose it with care, and do not overstate language levels, which recruiters check.
Komerční banka recommends a photo but says it is not required, in a plain setting and dressed as for an interview.
Jobs.cz says a CV should fit on two A4 pages at most and that graduates with little experience can usually manage with one; Komerční banka calls one A4 the ideal. Send it as a PDF.
EURES says a cover letter should be brief and focused on the job, and that larger companies may use their own questionnaire instead; the programmes read do not ask for one.
EURES lists references among the parts of a CV, but none of the programme pages read asks for them with the application; they come up later. This is our reading.
EURES advises bringing the CV and copies of certificates to the interview in a portfolio; certified copies are not mentioned.
Komerční banka’s CV advice says not to state salary expectations on the CV and to discuss pay at the interview.
EURES says some employers use a psychological test; we found nothing on routine background or reference checks for graduates.

Portals and programmes take open applications (Komerční banka also takes a CV when its programme is closed), while the surveys and pages read say nothing about the weight of introductions. This is our reading.

Red Hat’s Brno internship asks for enrolment at a Czech university, Komerční banka’s programme is for students in their 4th or 5th year, and EURES says nearly all employers require Czech; the English-speaking centres are the workable exception. This is our reading.
English in multinationals’ centres; EURES says the overwhelming majority of employers require Czech.
EURES says interviews are fairly formal, so dress appropriately, bring your CV and copies of certificates in a portfolio, and expect that some employers use a psychological test.

Red Hat asks applicants to apply to no more than three internship roles and to include education, projects with a GitHub link and extracurricular activities in the CV; incomplete applications may be left out of screening.

We did not establish the number of stages, the time from application to offer, the interview language outside the multinationals or assessment-centre norms: the Big Four and the other banks’ graduate pages were not served.
The employment contract must be in writing and you must receive a copy before starting; bilingual contracts are common, but the Czech version prevails legally.

EURES gives probation as up to four months (eight for managers), usually three, and the standard notice period as two months, starting on the first day of the month after notice is delivered. Full-time is 40 hours a week.

A year-end bonus or thirteenth salary is not universal: a Chamber of Commerce survey found 4 in every 10 private-sector firms planned one for 2023, almost 70% of large firms against 43% of medium-sized ones, most often between CZK 22,000 and CZK 46,000.
We did not establish whether graduates negotiate pay or how long employers give to decide.

For a non-EU hire the employer must enter the post in the Labour Office’s central register of vacancies; the 10–30 day waiting-period vacancy test was abolished on 1 July 2024, and the hire then goes on an Employee Card or, if paid at least CZK 73,823 gross a month, an EU Blue Card.
Graduates of Czech universities have free access to the labour market and a nine-month permit to look for work, so an employer can hire them without any filing of its own.

The employers with the HR capacity for this are the international service and technology centres, where about 43% of staff come from outside the country (ABSL). Ask early and ask whether the employer has filed an Employee Card before. This is our reading.
Portals: jobs.cz and profesia.cz, the Labour Office database via EURES, and LinkedIn; check that any agency holds a licence from the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs.
Employer pages: Komerční banka (kariera.kb.cz and traineeprogram.kb.cz), JetBrains internships, Red Hat university internships, and Škoda Auto’s Business, Tech and IT trainee tracks.
University services and fairs: Charles University’s Career Centre (careercentre.cuni.cz), VŠE’s ŠANCE (sance.vse.cz) and CTU’s Career Days.
Public sector: portal.isoss.cz for civil-service selection procedures.
Missing the spring window at Komerční banka: the page said the 2026 trainee programme was full and recruitment launches every spring.
Assuming English is enough: EURES says the overwhelming majority of employers require Czech, and the English-only roles are mostly in the international centres.
Overstating language levels or sending a long CV: recruiters check language levels, and Jobs.cz says two A4 pages at most.
Signing a bilingual contract without reading the Czech text: the Czech version prevails legally.
ABSL’s 2025 report says English is the common language of business in the service centres, which use many languages; EURES says nearly all other employers require Czech.
Komerční banka’s trainee and careers pages are in Czech and state no English or other language requirement.
Red Hat’s Brno internship asks for working knowledge of written and spoken English, and JetBrains’ internship page states no language requirement; Czech is not mentioned in either.
The civil-service selection procedures are published in Czech on ISoSS; we did not read a stated language level.
Eurostat’s figures show 86.1% of recent tertiary graduates aged 20–34 in work in 2025 (EU 85.3%) and youth unemployment of 10.4%. We found no return-offer or conversion rate for the Czech Republic.

Staying more than 30 days in private housing, report your address to the Foreign Police within 30 days of arriving; hotels and registered student residences do it for you. Missing it can be fined up to 3,000 CZK.

Entry-level job ads in Germany fell by about two-thirds from the 2022 record to mid-2026, against almost 39% for all ads; 26 of 28 occupational groups had fewer, with IT applications down 77% and marketing down 75%.
The unemployment rate of people with a degree was around 3% in 2024, up from about 2.5% in 2023, and the number of unemployed graduates averaged 290,000 in 2024 against 243,000 in 2023.
