The Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme for recent graduates has its next recruitment round in spring 2027, and Volvo Group’s 12-month Finance Graduate Program recruits next in autumn 2027.

Swedbank’s Analyst Development Trainee Program, for recent graduates in industrial economics, mathematics, economics, statistics or computer science, lasts over 10 months; applications are closed and open again in January 2027.
English is widely used in international workplaces in Sweden, but Swedish is an advantage and in many roles a requirement; CVs should be in the language of the job posting.
Graduate labour market
Entry pay
Sweden’s expert tax relief (25% of pay exempt for seven years) excludes anyone resident in Sweden in the previous five years, so it does not help someone who studied there.

Of SSE’s 2025 master’s class, 40% went into consulting, 29% into finance and 9% into technology, with first employers including McKinsey, BCG, SEB, Handelsbanken, Swedbank, Klarna and H&M; over 60% started their careers in Sweden and 38% of international graduates stayed.
SEB’s International Trainee Programme runs every other year from September; the 2026–27 intake closed on 11 January 2026, and some roles require Swedish.
AB Volvo has its headquarters in Gothenburg.

Eurostat counts 629,000 people in work in the Malmö metropolitan region in 2021: 25,000 in information and communication (third in Sweden, after Stockholm and Gothenburg) and 8,000 in finance and insurance (third in Sweden, after Stockholm and Gothenburg). The region’s GDP was €62.3 billion in 2021.

Eurostat counts 178,000 people in work in the Uppsala metropolitan region in 2021: 5,000 in information and communication and 1,000 in finance and insurance. The region’s GDP was €19.1 billion in 2021.

Eurostat counts 1,316,000 people in work in the Stockholm metropolitan region in 2021, 117,000 of them in information and communication (53% of Sweden’s 221,000) and 68,000 in finance and insurance (64% of 107,000).

Eurostat counts 870,000 people in work in the Gothenburg metropolitan region in 2021, 33,000 of them in information and communication (15% of Sweden’s 221,000) and 10,000 in finance and insurance (9% of 107,000).
Spotify gives its address as Regeringsgatan 19, Stockholm, as its headquarters, with entities in 16 countries.
Klarna gives its address as Sveavägen 46, Stockholm, and says it supports 26 countries.
Handelsbanken gives its head office as Kungsträdgårdsgatan 2, Stockholm, and says it has more than 12,000 employees.
Volvo Group says it has 99,000 employees, production in 17 countries and sales in 180 markets, with its headquarters in Gothenburg; Volvo Car Group gives Gunnar Engellaus väg 8, Gothenburg.
Axis Communications gives Lund as its headquarters and says it has around 5,000 employees in over 50 countries.
Uppsala University says it has 50,000 students and 7,539 staff (year average, 6,648 full-time equivalents).
In the QS World University Rankings 2027 (18 June 2026) Lund University is 71st, KTH 82nd, Uppsala University 87th and Stockholm University 167th, the first four in Sweden.

The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Stockholm 35th of 117 centres, the twelfth European centre after London, Zurich, Geneva, Luxembourg, Lugano, Paris, Copenhagen, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Dublin and Edinburgh, and 17th for fintech; Gothenburg is an associate centre with too few assessments to be ranked.

Startup Genome’s 2026 Top 40 ranks Stockholm 23rd in the world, level with Amsterdam-Delta and up eight places, the standout European performer; its Europe chapter names Amsterdam, Munich and Stockholm as the top tier after London, Paris and Berlin and puts Stockholm fourth in Europe for AI-native value ($5.8 billion, after London, Paris and Munich); the Stockholm page shows an ecosystem value of $56 billion against a global average of $25 billion.

Startup Genome’s Gothenburg ecosystem page shows an ecosystem value of $2 billion, $120 million of seed and Series A funding in 2023–2025 and $1 billion of exits, against global averages of $25 billion and $554 million.
In 2025 ICT specialists were 8.9% of employment in Sweden, the highest of the 33 European countries Eurostat lists (EU 5.0%, Luxembourg 8.7%, Finland 7.8%).

In 2025, 91.1% of Swedish tertiary graduates aged 20–34 who finished within the last three years were in work (EU 85.3%), but unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 24.3% (EU 15.2%), the highest of the Nordic countries.

In 2025 the average monthly salary of all employees was SEK 42,900 in Sweden, SEK 48,300 in the Stockholm region, SEK 42,300 in West Sweden (Gothenburg), SEK 41,700 in South Sweden (Malmö) and SEK 40,500 in East-Central Sweden (Uppsala).

Swedish hiring leans on contacts: many posts are filled through networks and referrals before they reach a job site, so career guides tell students to ask guest speakers for informational talks and go to alumni and industry evenings. Business graduates of the top school sign early: 80% of SSE’s master’s class accepted a job before graduating.
Partner companies, thesis and internships
SSE has more than 100 corporate partners and about a third of its graduates start with one of them.

Stockholm University tells students that internships help them understand Swedish workplace culture and recommends a master’s thesis written with a company, authority or organisation. Handelsbanken takes students into part-time jobs alongside their studies and lists thesis and internship options, and the Government Offices take unpaid interns of about 20 weeks twice a year.
Trainee and graduate programmes

Banks and industrial groups run trainee programmes with winter windows for an August or September start: SEB’s international programme took applications from November 2025 to January 2026 and runs every other year; Swedbank’s analyst programme (over 10 months) reopens in January 2027; Volvo Group runs a 12-month finance and a 15-month operations and engineering programme and welcomes 100+ graduates a year.
The Ministry of Finance runs a nine-month trainee programme for recent graduates with a permanent post from the start; its next round is in spring 2027.
Networks and referrals

Stockholm University says many jobs in Sweden are filled through networking rather than public adverts; it points students to guest speakers, classmates, alumni and career fairs. Informational interviews and LinkedIn contacts with alumni fill the posts that are never advertised.
Invest in Gothenburg advises personalised LinkedIn requests to peers and people in the target department, not asking strangers for jobs.
Posted vacancies

Expat.com says most vacancies are advertised online, with LinkedIn and company career pages the most widely used; Arbetsförmedlingen’s Platsbanken is open to everyone, but many international or specialist private-sector roles are advertised elsewhere.
This is also the route for the experienced hire: hiring slows in July, is mixed in August and picks up from September.
Campus career fairs

KTH lists 15 career fairs, led by Armada; LTH’s ARKAD brings about 200 companies and organisations to Lund over two days in November; Stockholm University runs career events and Chalmers works with Unimeet Gothenburg on company visits and a Career Day.
Recruitment and staffing agencies

Academic Work, founded in Sweden in 1998 for students and young professionals, has either recruitment jobs (you are employed by the client) or consultant jobs (you are employed by Academic Work and placed at a client); postings open to English speakers are tagged “Jobs in English”.
Expat.com says agencies matter mainly for specialised roles such as tech or finance, and are optional for most expats.
Graduates do well (91.1% of recent graduates in work), but youth unemployment is high at 24.3%: the gap falls on people without a degree or a network.

The big programmes open in the first months of the year for an autumn start, and many students apply in their final year rather than waiting for graduation. Examples: SEB’s intake closed on 11 January 2026, Swedbank’s opens again in January 2027, and the Ministry of Finance recruits in spring 2027.
Outside the programmes, recruitment can take several weeks or months to review, employers do not always tell unsuccessful candidates, and hiring slows in July.

Business graduates of the Stockholm School of Economics sign early: of its 2025 master’s class 40% went into consulting and 29% into finance, over 60% started in Sweden and 38% of its international graduates stayed.

KTH and Chalmers are the main feeders for engineering and IT; KTH’s Armada is described as Scandinavia’s biggest career fair, and Chalmers runs career services with workshops, drop-in sessions and one-to-one advice.

UHR, the Swedish ENIC-NARIC office, offers an assessment tool that gives a PDF comparing your education with Swedish education, which you can send to an employer; employers may not know a foreign university, so explain what you can do.
KTH lists 15 career fairs, and Armada, first on the list, is described as Scandinavia’s biggest career fair.

ARKAD at Lund University’s LTH takes place over two days in November with about 200 companies; LTH also holds a Career Day for international students (21 April 2026) on CV writing, job search in Sweden and work permits.
Stockholm University runs the Stockholm Student Academy, six evening sessions on Swedish society, culture and professional life, starting again in autumn 2026.

Banks recruit through trainee programmes with winter windows: SEB’s international trainee programme takes graduates of the last two years every other year, and Swedbank’s analyst programme (over 10 months) reopens in January 2027 for recent graduates in industrial economics, mathematics, economics, statistics or computer science. SSE sent 29% of its 2025 class into finance.

Handelsbanken lists several programmes for students and takes open applications for thesis and internships, contacting candidates when it sees a match; its summer jobs are advertised in the spring term.

The Big Four have large Swedish practices (EY has about 2,700 staff across 50 offices) and recruit graduates for August starts, including into technology consulting in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö.
Consulting took 40% and finance 29% of SSE’s 2025 class; McKinsey, BCG, Bain and the Big Four recruit on campus.

Industrial and consumer groups run trainee programmes that open from January to March for an August or September start; Lantmännen’s Graduate Trainee Program, which rotates new graduates through the business, came second among social-science students in Karriärföretagen’s 2026 student poll.
Volvo Group’s graduate programmes (Finance, 12 months, next recruitment in autumn 2027; Purchasing, Operations and Engineering, 15 months) are found by searching “Graduate” on its job site.

The Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme gives recent graduates a permanent post from the start, with visits to government agencies and EU institutions; the Government Offices’ internships of about 20 weeks are advertised in March and April and in September and October, are unpaid and include a security vetting for final candidates.

IT recruitment has slowed but stays strong, with an estimated shortage of about 18,000 professionals a year to 2028, mostly in AI, software and cybersecurity; at the same time Ericsson has cut thousands of Swedish jobs and Malmö’s games studios shed junior generalists. KTH and Chalmers are the main feeders.

Volvo Group’s Purchasing, Operations and Engineering programme suits people interested in IT and engineering; Academic Work places many graduates in IT and technology roles as consultants or direct hires.

Large employers open trainee applications in the first months of the year for an autumn start; SEB’s closed on 11 January 2026, Swedbank’s reopens in January 2027 and the Ministry of Finance recruits in spring 2027. Ordinary vacancies are posted all year, slowing in July.
The business-school pipeline is a master’s (80% of SSE’s class signed before graduating), but the programmes read name recent graduates without stating a degree level.

UHR, Sweden’s ENIC-NARIC office, assesses foreign qualifications for people seeking work and for employers, and its tool gives a PDF to send to an employer; for regulated professions it points to the authority responsible.
The top business school’s graduates sign early and KTH and Chalmers feed engineering, but the programmes read name no list of schools.

Students work part-time in the bank or firm alongside the degree (Handelsbanken), write the thesis with a company, or intern; there is no formal dual-study degree for business or computing graduates in the sources read.

The state offers a few graduate entries, such as the Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme and the Government Offices’ unpaid internships, but the large graduate programmes are in banks and industrial groups.

A work permit needs the job advertised in Sweden and the EU/EEA and Switzerland for at least ten days, pay at least on par with collective agreements and at least 90% of the median salary (SEK 34,470 a month from 1 June 2026). See Visas for the rules.
Many Swedish CVs carry a photo but it is not necessary; leave off the date of birth early in your career. Address the letter informally, by first name.
A Swedish CV is no more than two pages, and one is better; reverse chronological, no superlatives (“lagom”), and gaps such as parental leave are accepted.

The application includes a concise cover letter on why you suit the job and what you offer, not a repeat of the CV; it is usually in English with a note on your Swedish level, or in Swedish if the ad is.
Employers often ask for references before a final offer; do not list them on the CV but provide them when requested.
The sources read ask for a CV and letter; a UHR assessment PDF is the document to send when a foreign qualification is unfamiliar, and no source read asks for certified copies.
There is no statutory minimum wage and pay is set by collective agreements; when you name a figure, say it is flexible and negotiate benefits such as extra holiday. Offers are usually quoted gross.

References are checked for candidates who advance, and the Government Offices add a security vetting with an in-person interview for final candidates; no private-sector page read describes other checks.
Stockholm University says many jobs are filled through networking, while Expat.com says most vacancies are advertised online; both a posted application and a warm contact work.

Initial interviews are often remote, a CV in English is accepted unless you are truly comfortable in Swedish, and Invest in Gothenburg points to a job portal that filters English-speaking jobs; some trainee roles still require Swedish.

Applications in English are accepted at many firms, but specific roles at SEB and most local employers need Swedish; only 38% of SSE’s international graduates work in Sweden. English is widely used in international workplaces, but Swedish is an advantage and in many roles a requirement.

A typical process starts with a screening call, followed by one or two interviews and sometimes a test or case assignment; initial interviews are often remote, and processes can move quickly once they begin.

Employers assess cultural fit and look for people who work well in a collaborative, egalitarian environment; punctuality and preparation are valued. Dress is mostly smart casual, formal mainly in law and finance.

Programmes add steps: the Government Offices’ internship has an interview, reference checks and a security vetting with an in-person interview at the Government Offices in central Stockholm. Reviews can take weeks or months and unsuccessful candidates are not always told.

Standard Swedish contracts run until further notice; an employer may add a probationary period of up to six months, which either side can end during it (an employer gives at least two weeks’ notice) and which becomes permanent if no one ends it.

Special fixed-term employment is limited to 12 months within five years before it converts to permanent; collective agreements regulate wages, working time, pensions and notice periods beyond the statutory minimums.
There is no statutory minimum wage: the average is roughly SEK 40,000 to 42,000 a month before tax, and offers are quoted gross, so use the Tax Agency’s calculator for net pay.
The Ministry of Finance’s nine-month trainee programme comes with a permanent post from the start; you can name a flexible figure and ask what the company offers beyond salary.
The employer must advertise the vacancy in Sweden and within the EU/EEA and Switzerland for at least ten days, simplest on Arbetsförmedlingen’s portal, whose ads also appear on EURES.

Terms and pay must be at least on par with Swedish collective agreements and, from 1 June 2026, at least 90% of the median salary: SEK 34,470 a month, from a median of SEK 38,300 published on 16 June 2026.
Programmes read name no sponsorship policy; the one published language rule is SEB’s, where some trainee roles require Swedish, so ask early whether the employer has hired from abroad.

Posted vacancies: Arbetsförmedlingen’s Platsbanken, LinkedIn and employers’ own career pages; Invest in Gothenburg’s job portal filters English-speaking jobs, and Academic Work tags “Jobs in English”.

Missing the winter window: SEB’s intake closed on 11 January 2026 and runs only every other year; Swedbank’s reopens in January 2027.
Writing a formal, long or boastful application: keep the CV to two pages or fewer, avoid superlatives, address the letter by first name and leave off your date of birth.
Listing referees on the CV: provide references when asked, usually before a final offer.
Relying only on posted jobs: many are filled through networking, so talk to alumni and guest speakers; asking strangers for a job in the first message works against you.
Assuming English is enough everywhere: specific roles at SEB and most local employers need Swedish, and Swedish is common in informal workplace settings.
SEB’s international trainee programme works in English but some roles require Swedish; Swedbank’s programme page names no language requirement, and neither names a certificate.

Industrial groups such as Volvo and Lantmännen run programmes whose pages state no language requirement; Expat.com says English is widely used in international workplaces but Swedish is an advantage and in many roles a requirement.
Gothenburg’s job portal filters English-speaking jobs, so many tech roles are open in English; list your Swedish level even for English-language roles to show commitment.
The Ministry of Finance and Government Offices pages read name no English route; the state works in Swedish, so expect to need it.

Temasek, GIC, OCBC and UOB are not listed as employers because no head-office or headcount source we can cite was read.

Full-time employed residents with a degree had a median gross monthly income of S$9,038 in 2025, against S$5,775 for all full-time employed residents; the resident unemployment rate for professionals, managers, executives and technicians was 2.8%.

Bank graduate cohorts start in July: DBS’s Management Associate Programme commences on 5 July 2027 and HSBC’s Singapore corporate and institutional banking programmes start in July 2027, with assessment centres from September to November 2026; NTU’s main career fair runs each September and February, and the Employment Pass salary floor rises on 1 January 2027.

Singapore’s banks, consultancies and tech firms hire graduates through internships and graduate programmes recruited mostly from NUS, NTU and SMU. For a foreigner, the gate is the work pass more than the interview: the Employment Pass needs a salary of S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance), rising to S$6,000 (S$6,600) for applications from 1 January 2027, and 40 points under COMPASS.
Internship to graduate offer

UOB’s summer internship is a full-time placement of at least 10 weeks, and strong performers may be considered for its Management Associate Programme; DBS plans to hire more than 500 young local people in 2026 across its Management Associate, internship and traineeship programmes.
Internships also set pay: Deloitte’s starting pay of S$4,000 to 4,500 a month varies with internship experience.
No conversion rate from internship to offer was found in the pages read, so this ranking rests on the employers’ own programme pages, not on a survey.
Management-associate and graduate programmes

The local banks recruit one cohort a year: DBS’s Management Associate Programme is a 12-month permanent post that commences on 5 July 2027 with a full-day case challenge, UOB’s lasts 24 months, and HSBC’s Singapore corporate and institutional banking programmes start in July 2027 with assessment centres from September to November.

The Big Four take the largest classes: EY planned about 500 fresh graduates in 2025, roughly 75% from the autonomous universities, and PwC and Deloitte each hired more than 250; PwC drew more than 2,000 applications each cycle.
Career fairs and campus recruiting

NTU’s flagship career fair is held in September for the first semester and in February for the second, and SMU’s Career Fair is held twice a year with over 100 companies in accountancy, business, economics, information systems, law and social sciences.
Public-sector programmes

GovTech runs internships for polytechnic and university students, a Smart Nation Scholarship and a 3-year Technology Associate Programme; the Public Service Commission offers PSC Scholarships and a Master’s Scholarship that lead into the Public Service.
The Ministry of Education ranked second in gradsingapore’s 2026 list of leading graduate employers, behind DBS.
Apprenticeship-style programmes
AI Singapore’s AI Apprenticeship Programme trains engineers on real projects and says over 90% of its graduates are hired, by DSTA, DBS, Grab, Capgemini and AI Singapore itself.
OCBC Ignite, launched in 2024, combines internships and apprenticeships leading to full-time jobs and aims to benefit 500 polytechnic students and graduates over three years.
Direct application on MyCareersFuture and employer sites

Employers must advertise on MyCareersFuture for at least 14 consecutive days, with the salary range shown, before applying for an Employment Pass for a foreign hire, so experienced hires meet a public advert and a local-first process.
The salary floor sits above the median pay of local bachelor’s graduates (about S$4,500 to S$4,750), so outside finance, tech and consulting few entry jobs clear it.

Bank cohorts start in July of the following year (DBS on 5 July 2027), so selection runs in the second half of the year before: HSBC’s July 2027 programmes hold assessment centres from September to November 2026 on a rolling basis, and applications may close early.
The Employment Pass salary floor rises on 1 January 2027 to S$6,000 for most sectors and S$6,600 in financial services, for new applications.

The local banks run one intake a year through management-associate programmes: DBS, ranked the top graduate employer in 2026, planned to hire more than 500 young locals across its programmes; UOB’s programme lasts 24 months.

GovTech, the government’s technology agency, is among the top IT graduate employers, with internships, a Smart Nation scholarship and a Technology Associate Programme.

Information and digital technologies graduates had the highest median pay of any cluster in the 2025 survey, S$5,500 a month.

AI Singapore’s AI Apprenticeship Programme trains engineers on real projects and says over 90% of its graduates are hired, by DSTA, DBS, Grab, Capgemini and AI Singapore itself; Parliament has asked how many stay in-house.
COMPASS gives more points for a degree from a listed top-tier institution: NUS, NTU, SMU and a list of foreign universities and faculties.

In the points test, qualifications score 20 points for a top-tier institution and 10 for another degree-equivalent qualification, and verification proof is needed only if you claim those points; in hiring, EY took roughly 75% of its graduates from the autonomous universities.

NTU’s flagship career fair runs each September and February, and SMU holds its Career Fair twice a year with over 100 companies; the postgraduate fair at SMU, for students with more than two years of work experience, took place in February 2026.

Graduate applications ask for results rather than certified copies (HSBC sets a GPA minimum); certified proof comes later, at the work-pass stage, where MOM does not accept plain certificates and wants verified proof, with an English translation for non-English documents.
Employers publish bands: a MyCareersFuture advert used for an Employment Pass must show the salary range, and the maximum cannot exceed twice the minimum.

Qualification checks are routine at the pass stage: employers must ensure candidates’ qualifications are authentic and awarded by accredited institutions, and verification is needed once per candidate.

Hiring is public by design for foreign hires: the job must be advertised on MyCareersFuture for 14 consecutive days without an offer being made, and the MOM page warns against pre-selecting a foreigner and advertising only for show.

A foreign graduate needs an employer willing to apply for a pass and pay above the floor: S$5,600 a month today (S$6,200 in finance), 40 COMPASS points, and candidates below the salary are ineligible whatever their points.
English. Work-pass documents not in English must be uploaded with an English translation, and the programme pages read are in English.

The employer must clear the Fair Consideration Framework first: advertise on MyCareersFuture for at least 14 consecutive days and make no offer in that period, unless exempt (fewer than 10 employees, a fixed monthly salary of S$22,500 or more, a role of one month or less, or an intra-company transfer).

Then the pass: the salary must clear S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance) before COMPASS is even scored, and COMPASS needs 40 points from salary, qualifications, nationality diversity, local-employment support and bonuses.

Ask early whether the employer sponsors and at what level: over 80% of finance staff are local, and a starting salary of about S$4,000 to 4,500 sits below the floor, which is why this works mostly in finance, tech and consulting.
Portals: MyCareersFuture, the government job portal, and the employers’ own pages (DBS, UOB, HSBC, GovTech); gradsingapore publishes the ranking of leading graduate employers.

Ignoring the salary floor: an Employment Pass needs S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance), rising from 1 January 2027, and a candidate under the floor is ineligible whatever the COMPASS score.
Sending unverifiable qualifications: MOM does not accept plain certificates or notarised copies as proof, and screenshots from sources it cannot verify are rejected.

There is no single national graduate season: Deloitte’s Amplify internships for May to August 2025 closed on 30 March 2025, KBank’s 2024 Young Scholarship closed on 15 January 2024, and the civil service general-knowledge exam for 2026 took registrations from 14 January to 3 February 2026.

Among company hires recorded by the Board of Investment, the share of university graduates fell from 30.1% in 2018 to 17.2% in 2022 while secondary-school graduates rose from 41.1% to 57.3%; the NESDC report warns that new graduates may struggle to find jobs as demand falls.

Thai graduates enter through job portals (JobThai listed 121,450 jobs the day it was read), structured employer programmes and university co-operative placements; a foreign graduate needs an employer that can sponsor a work permit, which takes THB 2 million of paid-up capital and four Thai employees per foreigner unless the company is Board of Investment-promoted.

In the JobsDB hiring report for 2022-2023, seven in ten large organisations had hired recent graduates and more than half had taken interns. Several universities build a work placement into the degree, and employers say they use it to judge students before hiring.
Co-operative education and internship that turns into an offer

Walailak University runs an eight-month co-operative placement for all its programmes, with more than 2,500 students placed in fiscal year 2026 across more than 2,700 partner organisations; partner executives say the placement lets them assess students before considering them for future employment.

SCB runs a four-month co-operative programme for fourth-year students from leading Thai universities in data analytics and software engineering. No published rate of conversion from internship to offer was found for Thailand.
Graduate and management-trainee programmes

Central Group’s two-year Management Associate Program asks for a master’s degree in any field, an age of 28 or under and up to 3 years of work experience, and runs seven stages from an online test to an assessment centre.

Deloitte’s Amplify programme offered more than 100 twelve-week internships in Bangkok in 2025 and says interns who do well will be offered full-time jobs; KBank’s Young Scholarship sends scholars to a master’s abroad after three years of work at the bank.
Direct application through job portals

JobThai listed 121,450 jobs on the day it was read, with filters for new graduates, internships, AI jobs and salary bands; JobsDB is the other large board. In the JobsDB report, employers weigh the interview, the attitude to work and the field of study.
Campus recruiting and job fairs

JobsDB runs an annual campus programme with more than 20 universities (talks, a résumé clinic), and private fairs such as the WakuWaku Job Fair of 22 February 2025 in Bangkok held on-the-spot interviews for fresh graduates and experienced people.
Recruitment firms and the experienced hire

Recruitment firms such as Personnel Consultant advise checking company career pages regularly and keeping a profile with an uploaded résumé, so that recruiters can find you when suitable roles open. No survey of the share of experienced hires made this way was found, so the ranking is anecdotal.

In mid-2026 university graduates had the highest unemployment rate of any education level, 1.6%, while more than 300,000 vacancies were open: a mismatch more than a shortage. The graduate share of company hires fell from 30.1% in 2018 to 17.2% in 2022.
About 215,000 new bachelor’s graduates were expected to enter the labour market in 2025, and the Ministry of Labour put unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds at 5.89%, the highest of any age group.

Windows that were published: Deloitte’s May-to-August 2025 internships closed on 30 March 2025, and KBank’s 2024 scholarship closed on 15 January 2024. Central Group’s page gives no window. There is no single national season.

KBank recruits future leaders through its Young Scholarship: five full scholarships in the 2024 round for final-year students with a GPA of at least 3.25, who first work at the bank in wealth, credit or data for three years. SCB lists a special-programme page for new graduates, but its details could not be opened.
A career guide says the ACCA qualification is recognised in Thailand alongside the Thai CPA.
Supervising and auditing accounts is one of the occupations reserved for Thai nationals, so a foreign graduate cannot sign off audits in Thailand.

Retail and consumer groups run trainee tracks of their own: Central Group’s Management Associate Program is a two-year rotation in retail that ends in a leadership role, with an open house and an assessment centre in the selection.
Deloitte’s Amplify internships in Bangkok were open to graduating students from all disciplines and to graduates with under 3 years of experience; no page was read for the strategy firms in Bangkok.

New graduates report gaps in English, digital skills and soft skills; multinationals and Bangkok’s tech firms hire IT graduates, and SCB’s four-month co-operative programme puts fourth-year students on live software and data work.

No source read ranks Thai universities by employer demand. SCB takes co-op students from “leading Thai universities” without naming them, and Walailak places its students through the university itself.

JobsDB’s university activation visits more than 20 universities each year, and private fairs such as the WakuWaku Job Fair (22 February 2025, Grande Centre Point Terminal 21, Bangkok) offer on-the-spot interviews.
Job boards post vacancies all year and carry a “new graduate” filter; the programme windows found (Deloitte, KBank) are short and tied to an intake.

Central Group’s Management Associate Program asks for a master’s degree in any field. The other programmes found do not: Deloitte’s Amplify takes graduating students and graduates with under 3 years of experience, and KBank’s scholarship takes final-year students with a GPA of at least 3.25.

Accounting and auditing, Thai law, architecture and civil engineering are reserved for Thai nationals or Thai-licensed professionals (CPA, architect, engineer licences), with narrow exceptions for specialised expertise.

For a work permit the employer files a copy of your degree, and most jobs expect at least a bachelor’s degree. Until 28 February 2027 an Italian degree needs full consular legalisation, because the Hague Apostille does not yet apply.

Employers that run formal programmes recruit at universities they know (SCB names only “leading Thai universities”), but the hiring criteria in the JobsDB report are the interview, work attitude and field of study, not the school.
Co-operative education is common: Walailak places all its students for eight months, and SCB runs a four-month co-op. Both are placements arranged within a university programme.

The Office of the Civil Service Commission’s 2026 general-knowledge exam (Part A) offered 450,000 paper seats at 14 test centres, with registration from 14 January to 3 February 2026, for people who had finished or would finish a diploma, bachelor’s or master’s in the 2026 academic year. No figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hiring was found.
A company must have THB 2 million of paid-up capital and four Thai employees for each foreign employee it sponsors, unless it is promoted by the Board of Investment. See Visas for the rules.

The sources disagree: a Thai-language CV guide lists the photo as not necessary unless the employer asks for it, while a CV-builder guide calls a 3 by 4 cm headshot at the top right common and often expected. Include one when the advert asks, and use the same format.

A new graduate should keep the CV to one page; 1 to 2 pages is the range for 3 to 10 years of experience and up to 3 pages for executives. Give your name in Thai and English, and state your language levels.

No source read states whether a cover letter is expected. On the portals you apply with the profile and CV; write a letter when a programme asks for it or when you apply directly to a person. This is our reading.

Some employers check the past-employment references an applicant provides, and Thai law does not distinguish between checks before and after an offer; credential checks are standard practice at some firms.
A foreign graduate who needs a work permit must supply a signed copy of the degree, and until 28 February 2027 the degree needs translation and consular legalisation.

No source read states whether the application asks for an expected salary. JobThai offers salary-band searches (for example 100K and over), so have a figure in mind before you apply. This is our reading.

Background checks vary widely by employer and role. Education and licence checks are standard at some firms, criminal-record checks (through the Royal Thai Police, with your consent) are often skipped unless the role handles money or children.

Portals and programme pages take applications, and recruiters search uploaded résumé profiles; no survey of how much hiring runs through personal introductions was found, so this verdict is a judgement.

Work needs a Non-Immigrant B visa and a work permit that the employer files after you arrive, and the employer must meet capital and Thai-staff rules, so an offer is hard to land from abroad without a sponsor.

In the 2026 TOEIC survey 97% of Thai HR executives called English important and 80% used English assessments in recruitment; a CV-builder guide says Thai is the primary CV language, with an English version recommended for multinationals.
Central Group’s Management Associate Program has seven stages: application, online test, first interview, open house, assessment centre, final interview and onboarding.
English is tested: 80% of Thai HR executives in the ETS survey use English assessments in recruitment and screening, so expect a test or part of the interview in English.

No source read gives the time from application to offer or a dress code; Personnel Consultant advises researching the company and the role before an interview and being ready to discuss your experience, strengths, goals and motivation.
Probation typically lasts up to 119 days, because from 120 days an employee dismissed without cause is owed severance (30 days’ wages for 120 days to under 1 year, 90 days for 1 to under 3 years).

Notice is at least one pay period, typically 30 days, and a 13th-month salary is not required by law, so ask whether the contract includes a bonus. The minimum wage is THB 337 to 400 a day, depending on the province.
Whether a graduate can negotiate pay, and how long an employer gives to decide, was not established.

The sponsor must be a registered Thai company with THB 2 million of paid-up capital and four Thai full-time employees for each foreigner, unless it is promoted by the Board of Investment; the employer files the work permit after you enter on a Non-Immigrant B visa.

The employer must show the role cannot easily be filled by a Thai national, and some work is closed to foreigners whatever the permit: 39 occupations, among them accounting and auditing services and Thai law.
Because the employer must show the role cannot easily be filled by a Thai national, tell it early what Thai staff cannot offer: your language, your market or your specialist skill.
JobThai (jobthai.com) and JobsDB (th.jobsdb.com) are the large boards; JobThai has filters for new graduates and internships.

Programme pages: Central Group (careers.centralgroup.com), Deloitte Thailand’s Amplify internships, KBank’s scholarship page and SCB’s careers site. SCG, PTT and the other Big Four sites could not be opened.
University co-operative education offices place students with employers, and fairs such as the WakuWaku Job Fair take walk-ins.

Arriving on a tourist entry to interview and work: from 15 September 2026 visa-free entry for EU citizens is for tourism only, and starting work on a Non-B visa before the work permit is issued is a criminal offence.
Sending an Italian degree with only an Apostille before 28 February 2027, when Thailand still requires full consular legalisation.
Skipping the co-op or internship: it is how employers judge students before hiring, and graduates say their English, digital and soft skills are the gaps.
Aiming at a reserved occupation such as audit sign-off or Thai law: a work permit does not open it.

Employers in the Eastern Economic Corridor expect new hires to communicate in English first and learn technical English later; staff there mostly tested at A2 to B2. Hiring firms test English at recruitment (80% in the ETS survey), usually with the TOEIC.
IT graduates are asked for English at multinationals and Bangkok’s tech firms, and employers name English as one of the four skill gaps of new graduates.
Audit and accountancy services are reserved for Thai nationals, so the work is done in Thai with Thai-licensed professionals; the ACCA qualification is recognised alongside the Thai CPA.
A 2019 YouGov survey of 1,233 Thai graduates found that 52% worked in jobs unrelated to their degree, against 34% of those who had studied abroad; humanities graduates were the most affected, at 67%.

For a job, the company first gets the work permit pre-approval letter (WP.3); you then apply on thaievisa.go.th for the Non-Immigrant B visa, a 90-day single entry (€80).

Whoever houses you, landlord, host or hotel, must notify immigration within 24 hours (TM.30): private landlords often forget, which blocks your visa extension and brings a fine of 800 to 2,000 THB, so ask for the receipt in your first 48 hours.
Staying over 90 days, confirm your address every 90 days (TM.47), or pay 2,000 THB.

Do not start work on the visa alone: collect the digital work permit from the Department of Employment (3,100 THB) after a local medical check. In the last 30 days of the 90-day visa, apply for the one-year extension (TM.7, 1,900 THB).
The work permit needs a local medical certificate showing none of the 6 prohibited diseases, with a VDRL test (about 300 THB).

Before any trip abroad, get a re-entry permit (TM.8: 1,000 THB single, 3,800 THB multiple): leaving without one cancels your extension at the exit stamp. Avoid travelling during the 30-day “under consideration” period of an extension.

Of Turkey’s 189,636 bank employees at the end of 2025, 83,582 (44%) worked in Istanbul and 18,621 in Ankara; the state banks Ziraat, Halkbank and Vakıfbank give head-office addresses in the Istanbul Finance Centre at Ümraniye, and Akbank in Levent.

The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel within 10 km of the border with Syria because of fighting and a heightened risk of terrorism, and reports Iranian strikes in the wider region since 8 July 2026.

The US State Department rates Türkiye Level 2, exercise increased caution, because of terrorism, armed conflict and arbitrary detentions, and says not to travel to the border region with Syria and Iraq; it reports Americans detained on scant evidence and subject to exit bans.
Ankara had 18,621 bank employees at the end of 2025, the second-largest number after Istanbul’s 83,582.
Izmir had 9,943 bank employees at the end of 2025, third after Istanbul and Ankara.
Bursa had 4,714 bank employees at the end of 2025.

The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Istanbul 89th of 117 financial centres (101st in the March 2026 edition); in the region Dubai is 9th, Abu Dhabi 13th, Riyadh 46th, Doha 52nd, Kuwait City 60th, Bahrain 74th and Tel Aviv 94th.

Startup Genome ranks Istanbul third among emerging start-up ecosystems worldwide (Global Startup Ecosystem Report 2025), after a 423% rise in funding in 2024; its 2024 edition placed it fifth in Europe for affordable talent and in the top ten in Europe for funding.
Koç Holding, headquartered in Istanbul, ranks 203rd on the Fortune Global 500 of 2026, with revenues of $69,742 million and 120,219 employees.

TurkStat’s address-based population count at 31 December 2025 gives Turkey 86,092,168 residents, of whom 15,754,053 (18.3%) live in Istanbul, 5,910,320 in Ankara, 4,504,185 in Izmir and 3,263,011 in Bursa.

In 2024 Istanbul produced TRY 13,010.7 billion of gross domestic product, 29.2% of Turkey’s, ahead of Ankara with TRY 4,672.8 billion (10.5%) and Izmir with TRY 2,562.8 billion (5.7%); the five largest provinces made 53.0% of the total.
Gross domestic product per head in 2024 was $24,452 in Istanbul, $24,031 in Ankara, $16,949 in Izmir and $15,014 in Bursa, which ranked 13th among Turkey’s 81 provinces.

Turkish Aerospace (TUSAŞ) gives its headquarters as Kahramankazan, Ankara, with a research building at the METU Teknokent in Ankara and an office at the İTÜ ARI Teknokent in Istanbul, and runs student-team, university-industry and in-house start-up programmes.
The Aegean Free Zone (ESBAŞ), the operator says, exported $3.2 billion in 2025, up 12%, on a trade volume of $6.332 billion; it employed about 23,500 people and made 24% of Izmir’s exports.

Oyak Renault’s Bursa factory built 387,113 vehicles in 2025, of which 336,336 were passenger cars, and exported 271,994, about 14% more than in 2024; its chairman said more than 70% of output is exported.

In Turkey a degree no longer guarantees a job: 73.9% of bachelor’s graduates were in registered work in 2025, it took them 14.2 months on average to find a first job, and only 56.7% of those in paid work worked in their field. Large holding groups and banks run management-trainee programmes; elsewhere personal connections (tanıdık) open many doors.
Management-trainee and young-talent programmes

No survey ranks the routes in Turkey; this is first because the large employers found recruit this way, and the competition shows it: Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK 2026 received 58,036 applications from all 208 universities and took 252 people.

Akbank’s management-trainee programme takes students in their 4th year, master’s students and graduates of the last year; selection is an online application, a general aptitude test, interviews with assessment-centre exercises and then training, for posts in Ankara, Istanbul and Kocaeli.
Koç Holding’s Genç Yetenek programme takes undergraduates from the 2nd year and graduate students, and gives priority for internships at Koç Group companies after a summit and a competency inventory.
Personal connections (tanıdık)
At smaller and family-run firms, an introduction from someone who works there opens doors that a portal application does not. This is our reading; no survey was found.
Job portals and the public employment service

Graduates describe sending dozens of applications for little response: Bianet’s account quotes one who applied to more than 50 jobs and was mostly rejected because postings demanded three to five years of experience.

İŞKUR, the public employment service, lets job seekers register, search open and part-time listings and get counselling; Kariyer.net runs online Career Days on 27 October 2026 for students and new graduates.
Career fairs at universities

Bilkent University’s 28th Career Fair on 17–18 February 2026 listed 71 employers, among them Akbank, Garanti BBVA, Kuveyt Türk, Turkcell, Yapı Kredi, Ziraat Bankası, Türkiye İş Bankası, TUSAŞ, Beko and Nestlé Türkiye.
Internships, including the National Internship Program

The National Internship Program, run by İŞKUR under the Presidency’s patronage, lets university students intern at public bodies and private companies across Turkey; the Presidency’s Kariyer Kapısı portal links to it.
Koç’s programme routes participants into Koç Group internships and an Experience Programme that start in July.
Public-sector exams and state-bank recruitment

The public personnel selection exam (KPSS) is run by ÖSYM in separate sessions for graduates, associate-degree holders and secondary-school leavers; the 2026 graduate session had exams on 6, 12 and 13 September and results on 7 October.

Ziraat, Halkbank and Vakıfbank are not in the KPSS preference guide: they hire through their own announcements, written exams and interviews, and Ziraat’s 2026 posts did not ask for KPSS or ALES. Its spring 2026 call had 20 inspector-assistant posts, with a written exam on 10 May.

Spring is the main window: Akbank’s management-trainee applications closed on 30 March 2026, Koç’s Genç Yetenek ran from 26 March to 19 April 2026 with a summit on 5 May, results on 15 June and a start in July, and Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK evaluation began in January.
Fairs fall in winter and autumn: Bilkent’s was on 17–18 February 2026, and Kariyer.net’s online Career Days are on 27 October 2026.
Public posts follow ÖSYM’s calendar: the 2026 graduate KPSS exams were in September with results on 7 October, and placement preferences for the second round run from 17 to 24 December 2026.

Bilkent University’s fair draws banks, defence, industrial and tech employers to its main campus; Istanbul’s technical universities (ITU, Boğaziçi) and METU in Ankara are the usual sources for tech firms. This is our reading for the latter; we found no ranking of schools by employers.
Turkcell took applications from all 208 universities for GNÇYTNK 2026, and Koç’s programme is open to undergraduates from the 2nd year; neither names a school.
Kariyer.net Career Days: 27 October 2026, 11:00 to 17:00, fully online and free, for university students, new graduates and young talent; you must upload a CV and send the first message to a company.
Bilkent University Career Fair: 17–18 February 2026, about 70 companies, run by its Career and Alumni Office.
Koç Kariyer Zirvesi: 5 May 2026 in Istanbul, a one-day summit for selected Genç Yetenek applicants, free of charge.
Koç Holding’s Genç Yetenek programme covers the Koç Group’s companies; Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK hired 252 young people in 2026 into full-time and part-time roles.

The private banks (Akbank, Garanti BBVA, İş Bankası, Yapı Kredi, QNB) and participation banks such as Kuveyt Türk recruit final-year students and new graduates into management-trainee programmes with exams and fluent English.
Kuveyt Türk’s programme page (from 2018) starts with an English exam, then an evaluation centre with a simulation, presentation, group work and technical exam, then a panel with senior management.
The state banks recruit separately: Ziraat’s written exam includes English, and its 2026 call for 20 inspector-assistants set a birth-year limit of 1 January 1996 or later.

EY Türkiye recruits final-year students graduating in June, and recent graduates with 0 to 2 years of experience, in audit, advisory, tax and corporate finance (TAS); the 2026 listings we read (no longer online) named Istanbul, Ankara and Adana and asked for Turkish and English. We read no page for the other Big Four firms.
Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK added a data-centre Talent Camp with Google Cloud in 2026, with about three months of technical training.

Tech firms such as Trendyol mostly hire developers with experience: its 2021 backend hiring day asked for at least three years, with a 90-minute Codility test and then technical and HR interviews; junior roles exist but are few, and Istanbul’s technical universities (ITU, Boğaziçi, METU in Ankara) are the usual sources.
The Presidency’s Kariyer Kapısı portal carries public-sector job announcements and the National Internship Program; civil-service posts go through KPSS, state banks through their own exams.
The main programmes recruit in spring (Akbank to 30 March, Koç to 19 April), fairs fall in February and October and public exams follow ÖSYM’s calendar; there is no single national season.
Akbank takes 4th-year students, master’s students and recent graduates alike, and Koç takes undergraduates from the 2nd year and graduate students, so a master’s is not what decides.

YÖK, the Council of Higher Education, carries out recognition and equivalence of foreign degrees; the Ministry of Education says the equivalence certificate is compulsory for health-field graduates and for practising a profession on the basis of a foreign programme. The pages read do not say employers in other fields ask for it.

Kuveyt Türk’s 2018 programme page targeted graduates of “the leading Turkish universities”, while Turkcell took applications from all 208 universities; no ranking of schools by employers was found. This is our reading.

We found no dual-study or apprenticeship route into graduate jobs; the structured routes are management-trainee programmes and internships, including the National Internship Program. This is our reading.

ÖSYM runs KPSS in three degree levels, the Presidency’s portal carries public job announcements, and the state banks hire through their own exams; we found no figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hires, so the weight is our reading.

A foreign hire needs the employer to show five Turkish full-time insured staff per foreign worker, share capital of TRY 500,000 (or turnover or export thresholds) and pay at one to five times the minimum wage by role; micro-firms are rejected. Few graduate programmes look built for foreign hires. See Visas for the rules.
Kariyer.net says employers and HR specialists look at the photo on a CV and advises a clear, recent, plain-background portrait without selfies or filters; it does not call it compulsory.
Jobseeker says one A4 page is quite natural for students, new graduates and people with little experience, with two pages the general maximum, and that recruiters see it as normal.
The programme flows read (Akbank, Koç, Turkcell) run on an online form, tests and an inventory, with no cover letter mentioned. This is our reading.
None of the programme pages read asks for references with the application. This is our reading.
The programme pages read do not ask for certified or translated copies with the application; a foreign degree goes to YÖK for equivalence where that is needed. This is our reading.
None of the programme pages read states a salary or asks for an expectation; RehberPanda declines to give pay bands because unsourced ones mislead. This is our reading.

Some programmes screen by profile: Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK asks for third- and fourth-year students or graduates with at most two years of experience, and Ziraat’s inspector call set a birth-year limit; we found nothing on routine reference checks.
Portals and programmes take open applications, while smaller firms lean on introductions. This is our reading.

Akbank’s trainee post is fully on-site, Koç’s summit is a one-day event in Istanbul, and the public routes run through Turkish-language exams; a foreign hire cannot work on a tourist status and needs a work permit started through a Turkish consulate. This is our reading.

Turkish for nearly all roles; English is an asset in multinationals and is tested in the banks (Kuveyt Türk’s English exam, English questions in Ziraat’s written exam, where 60% is the pass mark for that section).

Akbank’s trainee process is an online application, a general aptitude test, interviews with assessment-centre exercises, then training; Kuveyt Türk’s (2018 page) starts with an English exam, then an evaluation centre and a panel. RehberPanda describes private-bank programmes as an online application, numerical-verbal-logical tests, an English assessment and an interview, sometimes with a group exercise and presentation.
Koç’s timeline in 2026: applications 26 March to 19 April, evaluation 19 to 27 April, summit on 5 May, a Korn Ferry competency inventory within two days, results on 15 June and a start in July.

Trendyol’s 2021 hiring day ran a 90-minute online Codility test, then technical and HR interviews on one online day, with offers after. We did not establish typical time from application to offer for the banks, interview dress norms or how common video interviews are.
Probation is at most two months (four by collective agreement) and either side can end the contract during it without notice or severance; written contracts are mandatory for terms of a year or more.

Notice is 2 weeks under 6 months of service, 4 weeks to 1.5 years, 6 weeks to 3 years and 8 weeks beyond; severance of 30 days of gross pay per full year is owed after one year. The legal week is a maximum of 45 hours.

The library’s visa guide records the 2026 gross minimum wage as TRY 33,030 a month. State-bank staff are not on the civil-servant pay scale: pay and benefits follow each bank’s own staff rules. We did not establish whether graduates negotiate, a thirteenth-month practice, or how long employers give to decide.

A foreign hire starts at a Turkish consulate with a signed contract and legalised degree, which issues a reference code; within 10 working days the employer files on e-İzin. The statutory time is 30 days, in practice 6 to 10 weeks. EU citizens cannot work on a tourist status or apply from inside Turkey without a residence permit of at least 6 months.

The employer must show five insured Turkish staff per foreign worker and capital of TRY 500,000 (or turnover of TRY 8,000,000 or exports of USD 150,000), and pay at least the minimum wage multiple for the role (1× for ordinary staff, 2× specialists, 4× engineers and architects). The Turquoise Card is a points-based route for the highly qualified.
Ask early and ask whether the employer has filed for a foreigner before; large groups and banks have the staff to do it. This is our reading.

Portals and public services: Kariyer.net (with online Career Days), İŞKUR (esube.iskur.gov.tr and the staj.iskur.gov.tr internship portal) and the Presidency’s Kariyer Kapısı (Kamu İş İlanları and the National Internship Program).
Employer programmes: Akbank’s management-trainee programme, Koç Holding’s Genç Yetenek, Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK and the Kuveyt Türk management-trainee page.
Public exams: ÖSYM (osym.gov.tr) for KPSS applications through its candidate system; the state banks’ own announcements.
University career offices and fairs: Bilkent’s Career and Alumni Office runs the February fair.
Waiting for the summer: the main trainee windows close in spring (Akbank 30 March, Koç 19 April), so the application comes the year before you graduate.
Treating English as a formality in banking: Kuveyt Türk starts with an English exam, and Ziraat’s written exam has 40 English questions out of 140.
Assuming the state banks use KPSS: Ziraat, Halkbank and Vakıfbank hire through their own announcements, and Ziraat’s 2026 posts did not ask for KPSS or ALES.
Sending a long CV: Jobseeker says one page is natural for new graduates and two the maximum.
Expecting to start as a tourist: an EU citizen cannot work on a tourist status or convert it in Turkey, and the permit starts at a Turkish consulate.

Kuveyt Türk’s trainee process starts with an English exam and only those who pass reach the evaluation centre (2018 page); Ziraat’s written exam has 40 English questions out of 140 with a 60% threshold for that section.
Akbank’s 2026 trainee page does not mention an English exam; its pages are in Turkish.
EY Türkiye’s 2026 audit and consulting graduate listings (no longer online) asked for Turkish and English; we read no page for the other Big Four firms.
Turkcell’s GNÇYTNK and Trendyol’s hiring day state no English requirement; their pages and processes are in Turkish and, for Trendyol, an online test and interviews. This is our reading.

TÜİK’s 2025 figures show 73.9% of bachelor’s graduates in registered employment (down from 2024), 14.2 months on average to a first job and 56.7% of paid-employed graduates working in a job matching their field. We found no return-offer or conversion rate for Turkey.

Graduates are often turned down because postings demand years of experience, and young women face far higher unemployment than young men: Bianet reports 16.2% youth unemployment in June 2025, 12.3% for men and 23.7% for women.

Master’s and PhD scholarships, TÜBİTAK and Türkiye Bursları included, are free of income tax.

To work, start the work permit through a Turkish consulate abroad: on visa-free entry you may not work or apply for a work permit inside Turkey unless you already hold a residence permit of at least 6 months. Students may enter visa-free and apply inside the country.
More than 1,169 neighbourhoods, including 10 whole districts of Istanbul, are closed to new foreign residents: a lease there means the residence permit is refused.

Students can join public health insurance (GSS) for 1,321.20 TRY a month, but must apply at the social security office within 3 months of first enrolling: after that the right is lost for the whole degree.

The application document keeps your stay legal until the decision but does not let you work. To travel while you wait, the fees must be paid and the document validated, and you may not stay abroad more than 15 days per trip, or the application is cancelled.

While a residence application is pending, each trip abroad may last at most 15 days; longer and the application is cancelled.
A residence permit never allows work: only a work permit, which the employer requests, does.
Overstay the 90 days and leave without paying the fine and you get a five-year entry ban.
Use only .gov.tr portals: agencies uploading false documents or addresses get you a five-year ban for fraud.

data/atlas/es/tw.js: German companies in Taiwan look for bilingual staff who can at least communicate in English, but graduates’ English is often only passive; returning graduates from abroad form a bilingual pool in high demand.

TSMC’s 2026 campus recruitment took applications to 30 April with interviews to 30 June, and its summer internship (6 July to 28 August) took applications to 8 May; the National Taiwan University campus fair was held on 7 March 2026 with 347 companies and more than 40,000 positions.
TSMC planned to hire around 8,000 engineers and technicians in 2026, and 104 Job Bank listed 21,762 finance, accounting and tax openings in May 2026, up 6.0% on a year earlier.

Taiwan’s unemployment rate was 3.32% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted) and 11.74% among 15- to 24-year-olds; 147,000 people entered the workforce in 2024, 5.3% fewer than in 2023, and 71.7% of them held a university degree and 19.5% a graduate degree.

Unusually open for graduates of its own universities: they can now stay up to two years after graduating and work in any job without a work permit. After that, a points test rewards pay and Chinese. Taipei is the finance capital: 35 of the 40 domestic banks have their head office there.

The Hsinchu Science Park Bureau oversees six parks where over 600 companies have been approved to operate, employing more than 160,000 people, with average annual revenue above NT$1,000 billion in recent years.
The Central Taiwan Science Park, centred on Taichung, had sales of over NT$936 billion in 2020 and more than 51,827 employees at 219 manufacturers.

No family is rated in Hsinchu or Taichung: the science-park figures read give companies and staff, not hiring by role. Tainan and Kaohsiung are not mapped: the Southern Taiwan Science Park and Kaohsiung port statistics could not be read.

Apart from the central bank’s lists of banks and insurers, TSMC is the only employer named, from its US Securities and Exchange Commission filing; MediaTek’s head office could not be confirmed from a source we can cite. No family is rated in Hsinchu or Taichung, so their standing rests on the science parks’ own statistics.

Taiwan’s statistics office publishes no GDP by city or county that was found, so no hub has a GDP figure; wages are the 2024 average annual total pay of full-time Taiwanese employees by workplace city (Hsinchu County, which shares the science park, is separate), population is the usual resident population, and Hsinchu has no Numbeo rent.
Country brief: three hubs, pay and standing
Entry pay
Pay across cities
The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Taipei 42nd of the centres it lists (rating 717), up nine places from 51st.

In 2024 the average annual total pay of full-time Taiwanese employees, by workplace, was NT$1,298,000 in Hsinchu City, NT$1,003,000 in Hsinchu County, NT$947,000 in Taipei City and NT$673,000 in Taichung City, against NT$776,000 nationally; the median was NT$902,000 in Hsinchu City, NT$735,000 in Taipei and NT$517,000 in Taichung.

In 2024 new entrants to the workforce earned NT$37,000 a month on average (up 6.4%): NT$34,000 for university graduates and NT$52,000 for graduate-school graduates; the median was NT$33,000, and NT$49,000 for graduate school.
On 1 January 2026 Taichung had 3,076,000 usual residents, Taipei 2,441,000, Hsinchu County 675,000 and Hsinchu City 509,000; the country had 23.71 million.

Graduates of Taiwanese universities who later need a work permit can qualify with 70 points, scored on degree, pay, experience, Chinese and languages; the Ministry of Labor formally abolished annual numerical quotas on 1 August 2024.
Whether employers expect Mandarin for entry roles was not researched; immigration rules, fees and tax are consolidated in visas_immigration/taiwan/.
The two-year permit-free stay took full legal effect under the amended Foreign Professionals Act on 1 January 2026 (WDA circular 4 Feb 2026).

Taiwan’s largest employers recruit graduates on campus: TSMC holds job fairs at the main universities each year for students graduating that year, alongside summer internships for enrolled students, and the National Taiwan University fair of 7 March 2026 had 347 companies offering more than 40,000 positions. Most other hiring runs through local online portals, of which 104 Job Bank is the standard for specialists.
Campus recruitment drives and career fairs

TSMC’s campus drive is open to bachelor’s, master’s and PhD students graduating in 2026 or able to start by the end of the year; applications ran to 30 April and interviews to 30 June. It also plans visits to National Taiwan Normal University and Taipei Tech.

The National Taiwan University “VISION 2026” campus fair on 7 March 2026 had 347 companies at 450 booths and more than 40,000 positions, a record for the university; 70% of the companies offered cross-disciplinary roles. EY was there, recruiting 2026 graduates for audit, tax, financial accounting advisory and technology risk.
Management-associate programmes at financial groups

Financial groups recruit through management-associate (MA) programmes on campus fairs in March. In the 2017 season Fubon was taking about 30 recruits, CTBC more than 50, First Bank about 60 reserve officers and E.SUN 500 hires plus 30 MA and TMA places; SinoPac required TOEIC 750 and First Bank TOEIC 900. Those figures are from 2017.
Pay in the programmes was quoted as reaching or exceeding NT$1 million a year for the best-paid tracks (Cathay, Fubon, China Life), not guaranteed for every MA role.
Summer internship that turns into an offer

TSMC’s summer internship ran from 6 July to 28 August 2026, with applications to 8 May and interviews to 29 May; it requires enrolment, accepts undergraduates from the third year and prefers master’s and PhD students, and strong interns may receive full-time offers.
A Taiwanese-degree graduate can also take an internship after graduating by extending the residence permit for that purpose; the NTU career centre handles eligibility.
Online job portals

Local online portals are the main recruiting channel: 104 Job Bank is the standard for specialists and managers, with 1111 Job Bank, 518 Job Bank and Yes123 as other local boards, LinkedIn growing for international roles, and Cake.me and Yourator posting in several languages. 104 listed 21,762 finance, accounting and tax openings in May 2026, up 6.0% on a year earlier.
Companies often use the messaging app LINE to arrange interviews and make first contact.
Work first on the job-seeking stay (Taiwanese-degree graduates)

A graduate of a Taiwanese university can extend the residence permit for up to two years to look for work and may work freely in that time without a work permit, full-time or part-time (Workforce Development Agency circular of 4 February 2026). This is how foreign graduates start in jobs and internships that would otherwise need a permit.
Experienced hires: portals, LinkedIn and the Employment Gold Card

Experienced foreign professionals can use LinkedIn and the Talent Taiwan portal; the Employment Gold Card is a 4-in-1 permit that allows a change of job or freelance work without employer sponsorship. German companies in Taiwan look for bilingual staff, and returning graduates from abroad are a bilingual pool in high demand.
The overall unemployment rate was 3.32% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted), but 11.74% among 15- to 24-year-olds. TSMC planned to hire around 8,000 engineers and technicians in 2026.
Competition for accounting graduates is pushing pay up: in May 2026 the Big Four raised audit-department pay by about 9% (PwC), at least 10% (Deloitte) and about 12% (EY and KPMG) on average.
New entrants to the workforce numbered 147,000 in 2024, down 5.3% on 2023.

Taiwanese financial groups recruit on campus through management-associate (MA) programmes; the Anue report on the 2017 season names Cathay, Fubon, CTBC, Shin Kong, Yuanta, SinoPac, China Life, E.SUN, First Bank and KGI Bank among the firms at the campus fairs.

The Big Four compete hard for audit graduates: in May 2026 they raised audit pay by about 9% to 12% on average, KPMG and EY raised new-graduate starting pay by NT$2,000, Deloitte by 5% and PwC by an unspecified amount. KPMG said high performers could reach NT$1 million a year within two to three years.

At the NTU fair of 7 March 2026, 70% of the 347 companies offered cross-disciplinary roles, and TSMC’s own campus drive lists business and accounting among the majors it recruits, next to engineering and computer science.

TSMC planned to hire around 8,000 engineers and technicians in 2026 and offered master’s-level new hires an average of NT$2.2 million a year; it recruits through campus fairs at National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University and Taipei Tech, and its summer internship prefers master’s and PhD students.

Employers recruit at named campuses: the 2017 financial-group fairs were at National Taiwan University (5 March), Tsinghua (18 March) and National Chengchi University (24 March), and TSMC’s 2026 visits listed National Taiwan University, National Taiwan Normal University and Taipei Tech.

For the work permit, graduates of the top 200 universities can use a streamlined application for specialised professional work, according to NTU’s international office; the criteria are on the EZ Work Taiwan portal.

The NTU campus fair “VISION 2026” on 7 March 2026 is the largest in the year, with 347 companies and 450 booths; TSMC also holds information sessions, in person or online, which students register for on the university’s site.
The financial groups’ management-associate fairs ran in March in the 2017 season, at three universities within three weeks (5, 18 and 24 March).

A spring peak of campus fairs (NTU on 7 March 2026) and application windows that close in April and May (TSMC campus recruitment 30 April, internship 8 May), with online portals carrying openings through the year.

New entrants with a graduate degree earned NT$52,000 a month on average in 2024, against NT$34,000 for university graduates; TSMC’s summer internship prefers master’s and PhD students, and master’s-level new hires averaged NT$2.2 million a year.

No recognition centre screens degrees for ordinary jobs. For the work permit the employer files the degree with the Workforce Development Agency, which reads a master’s as needing no experience and a bachelor’s as needing two years; a degree from a top-1,500 university waives the experience.

Recruiters go to named campuses (NTU, Tsinghua, Chengchi, Taiwan Normal, Taipei Tech) and the work-permit rules favour top-200 universities, but no page we read says how far the university name decides who is interviewed.
University graduates reach employers through campus recruiting, internships and portals; apprenticeship or dual-study contracts are not a route we found in any source for university graduates.

We found no page on public-sector graduate hiring in Taiwan; the sources read describe private employers (TSMC, financial groups, the Big Four) as the graduate route, so we rate the public sector small for a foreign graduate.

The ordinary work permit needs NT$47,971 a month in pay, and the sponsor needs paid-in capital of at least NT$5 million if under a year old or turnover of at least NT$10 million; science-park firms and certified innovative start-ups are exempt from the size tests. Taiwanese-degree graduates score on a points test instead, with no salary floor. The rules themselves are under Visas.
A photo is common on Taiwanese résumés, in our reading; the Taiwanese interview can also touch on family and private life, which GTAI says is not taboo.
Applicants usually submit a CV and a cover letter, often through a portal’s structured résumé. We found no page that sets a length; treat two pages as our reading.
GTAI says applicants usually submit a cover letter with the CV, then are invited to interviews.
Unlike in Germany, employers rarely ask for references or former employers, according to GTAI.

For a work permit the employer files the degree, and the Admetia library notes that Italian diplomas go through the consular legalisation chain of the Taipei office in Rome or Milan, not an apostille.
Taiwanese résumé forms usually include an expected-salary field, in our reading; pay is the top incentive at every level, according to GTAI.
No page we read says how routine background or reference checks are; GTAI says employers rarely ask for references.
Portals and campus drives take applications directly, and LINE is used to schedule interviews; we found no page showing referrals as the main door.

A foreigner abroad needs an employer that files for the work permit, with NT$47,971 a month in pay and two years of experience for a bachelor’s; Taiwanese-degree graduates have a two-year permit-free job-seeking stay that applicants from abroad do not.

Chinese counts for up to 30 of the 70 points in the graduate points test, and many positions require it; German companies look for staff who at least communicate in English, though graduates’ English is often passive. English-only roles are mostly in semiconductor engineering and foreign firms.

GTAI describes the usual sequence as a CV and cover letter, then interviews, mostly in person; technical tests, sales presentations and panel rounds are typical next steps, and companies use LINE to arrange them.

TSMC’s campus process is an online application on its portal, then interviews for shortlisted candidates: in 2026 applications ran to 30 April and interviews to 30 June, about two months. For the summer internship, applications ran to 8 May and interviews to 29 May.
Interviewers may ask about family members and family planning, which GTAI says is not taboo in Taiwan; phone and online interviews are less common than in-person ones.
The management-associate tracks at financial groups were quoted with English-test floors in 2017: TOEIC 750 at SinoPac and TOEIC 900 at First Bank.

After three months of service an employer ending a contract under the Labor Standards Act must give 10 days’ notice up to one year of service, 20 days from one to three years and 30 days after three years, or pay wages for the notice period. Severance is one month’s average wage per year of service, and a worker may take paid time off to look for a job during the notice period.

Entry pay is modest and uniform: new entrants averaged NT$37,000 a month in 2024, and 18.7% started at the basic wage of NT$27,470 (19.7% of university graduates and 3.5% of graduate-school graduates).
Among 2023 entrants still employed in December 2024, about 80% of the cohort, average pay had risen 15.7% in a year, from NT$36,000 to NT$42,000.
A foreign employee is enrolled in the National Health Insurance from the first day of work, the employer arranging it.

The sponsoring company must meet size tests: paid-in capital of at least NT$5 million if under a year old, or average turnover of at least NT$10 million, with science-park firms and certified innovative start-ups exempt. A start-up that does not meet them is rejected automatically.

The employer files on the EZ Work Taiwan portal with the contract, the degree and references; the work permit takes 7 to 10 working days and the whole route four to six weeks. Offer the employer a candidate who meets the NT$47,971 floor, or who is a Taiwanese-degree graduate scoring 70 points.
What an employer wants to hear is Mandarin ability (the points test gives 30 points for C2, 25 for B2 and 20 for B1 on the TOCFL) and a salary at or above NT$47,971, which scores 40 points.
