Across the United States in May 2025 there were 1,687,890 software developers (mean pay $148,100), 361,980 financial and investment analysts ($116,800), 262,440 data scientists ($126,800), 898,280 management analysts ($113,790) and 1,449,500 accountants and auditors ($94,750).

Goldman Sachs’s 2027 Summer Analyst Program in the Americas is a nine-to-ten-week internship for undergraduates, usually taken in the third or penultimate year of study; applications for some businesses were open when read.

About 197,300 people work in New York City’s securities industry (219,100 in the state), and 1 in 13 New York City jobs is directly or indirectly tied to it; the industry paid $6.7 billion, 8.4% of city tax revenue.
New York City’s securities industry employed a record 201,500 people in 2024, with an average bonus of about $247,000 forecast for 2025.

The Bay Area remains the top tech talent centre in the United States, both in the number of tech jobs and in the tech sector’s share of regional employment; between 2021 and 2024 tech jobs grew 10% there, against 26% in Dallas, 25% in South Florida and 16% in Charlotte.

The 20 largest tech companies in Silicon Valley and San Francisco employed about 215,000 people in mid-2025, 9% of the region’s workforce; the largest are Google, Apple, Meta, Amazon, Cisco and Tesla, and in 2025 Google cut 4,000 Bay Area jobs while NVIDIA added 1,000.

Silicon Valley and San Francisco companies drew about half of all US venture capital in 2025 (49%); AI companies took nearly $80 billion, 83% of the region’s total, and San Francisco’s share of the regional total rose to 62%.

Silicon Valley still hosts about half of US unicorn companies, produced over 23,000 utility patents in 2025 (17% of US patent assignees), and its tech workforce includes nearly 140,000 software developers.

Twenty-seven Fortune 500 companies are headquartered in the Houston area, among them Exxon Mobil (rank 9), Chevron (21), Phillips 66 (29), Sysco (55), ConocoPhillips (75), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (133) and Baker Hughes (164).

Dallas–Fort Worth has 24 Fortune 500 headquarters in 2026, among them McKesson (a Fortune 10 company), AT&T (35), American Airlines Group (86), CBRE Group (118) and Texas Instruments (252); seven are on the Global 500.

Chicago is the headquarters of Archer Daniels Midland (Fortune 500 rank 58), United Airlines (81), McDonald’s (170), Kraft Heinz (184), Exelon (189), GE HealthCare (217) and Motorola Solutions (378); Illinois has 29 Fortune 500 companies.

The Charlotte region is the headquarters of Bank of America (Fortune 500 rank 20), Lowe’s (52), Honeywell (116), Nucor (142), Duke Energy (145) and Truist (150); it has 46,000 jobs in headquarters and company management, about twice what its size would suggest.
Metro Atlanta has 14 Fortune 500 headquarters, according to the state’s economic-development site, which names The Home Depot, Mercedes-Benz USA and Porsche among the companies based there.
Amazon employs about 49,000 people in Seattle (down from 60,000 in 2020) and about 15,000 in Bellevue, and the University of Washington has overtaken it as Seattle’s largest employer.

Federal employment in the Washington region fell from about 375,800 jobs at the start of 2025 to 312,500 by May 2026, the lowest in 30 years, and the metro lost 100,500 jobs in all between May 2025 and May 2026.
Amazon’s second headquarters in Arlington, Virginia, announced on 13 November 2018, commits more than $2 billion and at least 25,000 jobs by 2030; the first phase was finished in spring 2023.
Boston-Cambridge ranks first among US biopharma clusters in 2026, with 117,108 jobs, $6.85 billion of venture capital in 2025 and 7,037 NIH awards worth $4.339 billion.

Eight Philadelphia-area companies were on the 2025 Fortune 500, led by Cencora (rank 10) and Comcast (35), then Lincoln National (228), Aramark (239), Universal Health Services (271), Toll Brothers (390), Burlington (399) and Campbell’s (419).
Greater Philadelphia ranks fifth among US biopharma clusters in 2026, with 88,000 jobs, $1.31 billion of venture capital in 2025 and 3,201 NIH awards worth $1.94 billion.

Miami-Dade’s finance sector has more than 150,000 jobs and about $28 billion of gross regional product; more than 60 international banks operate in Brickell, and Citadel has moved its headquarters there.

Los Angeles County’s economy exceeds $1 trillion and grew 2.4% in 2025, though the county has lost about 400,000 residents since before the pandemic and the 2028 Olympics are projected to add up to $18 billion.

Referrals carry the screen: in one large firm, referred applicants were 6% of applicants but 29% of hires.

For a European without US work rights the door is narrow: international students’ post-graduation employment is 44.6% against 62.1% for domestic peers, and many campus employers have policies against visa sponsorship.
Summer internship to return offer
In-person internships convert far better than hybrid ones: an average offer rate of 72% against about 56%.

The offer rate for the 2024 intern class was 62% across 247 responding organisations, the lowest in five years; international students are 30% less likely to get an offer from their internship employer and only 25% of them complete off-campus internships, against 42% of domestic students.
On-campus recruiting

Banks, consultancies and large firms send recruiting teams to a list of target schools, collect CV books, hold presentations and run first-round interviews on campus; students elsewhere compete in the online pool.

The timing is early: tech postings open from July, the Big Four from August to October, consulting from March to August the year before, and investment banking from December to March for the following summer.
Networking and referrals
Informational calls with alumni, then a request to pass the CV on, are the standard way to reach firms that do not visit your school.
The advantage is concentrated at the interview stage: referred applicants were 6% of applicants, 21% of interviewees and 29% of hires, so a referral gets you read but does not decide the offer.
Posted openings, rotational programmes and start-ups

Most large employers take applications on their own career sites and judge them as they arrive: Deloitte lists internships, full-time roles and a two-year Corporate Finance programme, and JPMorganChase runs four stages (explore, apply, interview, decision) with several people over multiple rounds.
Start-ups recruit later, from December 2026 to March 2027 for summer 2027, and are a fallback if the fall cycle failed; most big employers stop reading once their pipeline is full.
Federal government (Pathways)

The federal Pathways Program has an Internship Program (480 hours, conversion within 180 days after the degree) and a Recent Graduates Program for degrees completed within two years, applied for on USAJOBS; non-citizens can be appointed only if lawful permanent residents or otherwise authorised to work, and noncompetitive conversion needs US citizenship.
Company transfer
Routes that need no US degree exist, among them the intracompany L-1 visa, so an employee of a multinational can move to its US office after working for it abroad; see Visas for the rules.

Employers’ plans for the class of 2026 swung from flat in the autumn to a 5.6% rise in the spring update, led by large firms (employers with over 5,000 staff plan 8.7% more); the intern offer rate for 2024 interns was the lowest in five years.
Summer 2027 applications opened in waves: finance from December 2025 to March 2026, consulting from March to August 2026, tech from July 2026 and the Big Four from August to October 2026.
The graduate market is soft: recent graduates had an unemployment rate of about 5.6% in the second quarter of 2026 against 4.3% for all workers, and 42% were underemployed.
Wall Street recruits summer analysts six to twelve months earlier than London; non-target applicants are under a tenth of junior classes and rely on cold emails and alumni referrals.

Goldman Sachs’s 2027 Summer Analyst Program is a nine-to-ten-week internship for undergraduates in the third or penultimate year, and the one-year finance master’s at MIT reported 97.1% of job seekers with an offer within six months.
The Big Four recruit accounting graduates through campus internships, but PwC US planned to cut entry-level hiring by almost a third over three years as AI and offshoring take on junior audit work.
CPA licensing is set by each state, and the 150-hour rule is being replaced: 39 jurisdictions had signed changes by October 2026, so check your state board’s route before planning a fifth year.

Strategy firms recruit on the same target campuses as the banks (the Ivy-Plus colleges, Berkeley, Michigan, Virginia), mostly from summer internships, and hire MBAs from the top business schools a level above.
Bain starts with a digital assessment and then case interviews, adds behavioural questions, and for technical roles a coding challenge; its summer windows run into late August.
Brand management at consumer-goods firms is filled mostly from MBA summer internships; pre-MBA graduates enter through sales and analyst roles. Marketing hiring at big tech fell 36% against 2019.
Corporate programmes are tied to the internship: Deloitte lists a two-year Corporate Finance programme that gives investment-banking experience before business school or private equity.
Federal hiring of graduates goes through USAJOBS and Pathways; federal employment in the Washington region fell from about 375,800 to 312,500 between January 2025 and May 2026.

New-graduate hiring at big tech is about 65% below 2019, and graduates of the top 20 computer-science programmes are 45% less likely to land a job at a major tech firm than earlier cohorts. Software postings are recovering, but 71% of the rebound is senior roles.
Big tech recruits through internships, hackathons and coding contests, heavily from Stanford, MIT, Carnegie Mellon, Berkeley and other top computer-science departments.
Amazon had the most new H-1B approvals in fiscal 2025 (4,644), followed by Meta (1,555), Microsoft (1,394) and Google (1,050): large tech firms are where a sponsored software job is most likely.
Quant and AI research teams hire from a short list of mathematics and computer-science departments, and decide on coding tests and technical interviews more than on the school.
Federal security agencies and defence contractors hire many entry-level cyber staff, but most posts need US citizenship and a security clearance.
The target effect is causal: attending an Ivy-Plus college instead of a strong public flagship triples the chance of working at a prestigious firm.

Non-target applicants are under a tenth of junior classes at the banks; a one-year US finance master’s such as MIT’s or Duke’s is a way into the recruiting machine, though Duke’s international graduates needing a visa had a 71% offer rate at six months against 85% for those with work rights.
Autumn career fairs, firm presentations and invitation-only dinners on target campuses; hackathons and coding competitions for tech.

Deloitte runs case competitions for students: a Consulting National Undergraduate Case Competition with local on-campus rounds leading to a national final, a tax case (FanTaxTic) and a competition for advanced-degree students.
Peak posting months for big tech and the Big Four are September and October, when fall career fairs also happen.

Each industry has its own window the year before the job starts: investment banking December to March, consulting March to August, tech July to February, the Big Four August to October; most big employers read applications as they arrive and stop when the pipeline is full.

An MBA fills brand management and the consulting level above the undergraduate class, and one-year specialist master’s (MIT MFin, Duke MMS) feed recruiting machines, but most entry roles are open to bachelor’s graduates.

Only licensed professions need recognition, each through a state board: a CPA licence is set by the state board of accountancy, and 39 jurisdictions have signed changes to the 150-hour rule. For other jobs, employers can verify education through background checks.
The target effect is causal: attending an Ivy-Plus college triples the chance of working at a prestigious firm, and elite firms concentrate hiring on a few schools.

The American counterpart of dual study is the internship and co-op, with JPMorganChase also listing apprenticeships among its entry routes; the federal Pathways Internship hires students for up to a year initially, or longer to finish their studies.

The federal government hires graduates through Pathways on USAJOBS, but federal employment in the Washington region fell from about 375,800 to 312,500 between January 2025 and May 2026, and the largest graduate classes are in banks, consultancies and tech.

NACE’s legal guidance says many employers, especially on campus, have policies against visa sponsorship while thousands of others have no concern about it; employers may ask only whether you are authorised to work and whether you will need sponsorship now or in future. See Visas for the rules.
Never add a photo or date of birth; a one-page résumé with grades (GPA) shown.
A one-page résumé for students in finance and consulting, with GPA always shown; omitting it signals a bad grade.
The pages read (Goldman, JPMorgan, Deloitte, Bain) describe an online application and interviews, not a compulsory cover letter; the résumé is the document that gets read.
References are not part of the first application at the employers read; they are asked for late in the process, alongside the background check.
Transcripts are rarely required with the first application; education is verified later through the background check.

At least 13 states plus DC require pay ranges in job postings (California, Colorado, New York and Washington among them), and states such as California, Maryland and Oregon bar employers from asking about pay history, so the number comes up in the offer stage and the posted range is your anchor.

Employers must give a stand-alone written notice and get written permission before ordering a background report, and may look into work history, education, criminal record and more; they must send a notice before rejecting someone on its basis.
Applications are online, but referrals decide who gets read; alumni are the most useful contacts.
Without a US degree and its work permission after study, a European graduate needs an employer to sponsor a visa, which most entry-level programmes do not do.
International students apply to about twice as many jobs and receive 30% fewer offers.
English.

Finance and corporate programmes run in stages: Goldman Sachs uses an application, a video interview of about 30 minutes, then two to five interviews of 30 to 60 minutes (a search summary of its student pages); JPMorganChase says to expect several people in multiple rounds and may add a recorded on-demand video interview.

Consulting: Bain runs a digital assessment, then case interviews and at least one behavioural interview, and sometimes a take-home assignment with about three days to complete it; technical roles can have a coding challenge.
Interviews are in English, and the pages read give no typical time from application to offer; many employers judge applications as they come in.

Termination is generally governed by private or labour contracts unless it involves discrimination or whistleblowing, and federal law does not require paid vacation, sick leave or holidays: these are matters of agreement, with state laws on top. Read the offer letter for leave, health insurance and any probation or notice terms.
Medical questions generally cannot be asked before a conditional job offer, and the offer is typically conditional on a background check and proof of work authorisation.
Conversion of interns averaged 63.1% in NACE’s 2026 report; the pages read do not say how long you have to decide on a full-time offer or how far pay can be negotiated.

Employers may ask two questions: whether you are legally authorised to work in the US for any employer, and whether you will now or in future require visa sponsorship. NACE’s guidance advises answering the second honestly, usually yes, because most international graduates will need H-1B sponsorship after OPT.

Many on-campus employers have policies against sponsorship, while thousands of others have no concern; students may need to look beyond employers that recruit on campus. The biggest new H-1B sponsors in fiscal 2025 were Amazon (4,644), Meta (1,555), Microsoft (1,394) and Google (1,050).

Universities and non-profit research bodies can sponsor outside the H-1B cap, and the cap lottery is weighted by wage level from fiscal 2027; so an employer’s willingness depends on pay level and organisation type. See Visas for the rules.

Employers’ own career sites are the main route: apply.deloitte.com for Deloitte’s internships and full-time roles, the JPMorganChase and Goldman Sachs student pages, and Bain’s hiring pages; most take applications as they arrive.
Federal jobs: USAJOBS, with the Federal Internship Portal (intern.usajobs.gov) and the Recent Graduate Portal (recentgrad.usajobs.gov) for Pathways.
Campus: career-services fairs and firm presentations on target campuses each autumn, and the university’s alumni network for informational calls.
Data on who sponsors: the USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub shows which employers get approvals, as in the fiscal 2025 analysis by the National Foundation for American Policy.
Applying late: finance postings open from December, consulting from March, tech from July and the Big Four from August, and most employers stop reading once their pipeline is full.
Sending a European CV: a photo, date of birth or a two-page Europass; the American résumé is one page with GPA shown.
Treating a referral as the whole job: it raises the chance of an interview (6% of applicants, 21% of interviewees), but offers still depend on performance.
Hiding the sponsorship question: NACE warns that saying no to hide the need could make an employer question your honesty, and recommends being up front.
Skipping the internship: employers made full-time offers to 62% of their 2024 interns, so an internship is the main entrance, and an in-person one converts best (72%).
American finance recruiting is in English, from the video interview to the final rounds; no certificate is asked, the interviews are the test.
Bain’s case and behavioural interviews are conducted in English, and the cases test structured thinking and communication; no language certificate is named.
Corporate programmes such as Deloitte’s are in English; another language is an asset in roles serving other markets but is not asked for in the pages read.
Technical screens are in English and test coding: Bain’s technical roles use a coding challenge, and Goldman’s engineering interviews add HackerRank or CoderPad.
Employers made full-time offers to 62% of their 2024 interns, down from two-thirds in 2023 and the lowest in five years; the 2026 report shows an average conversion rate of 63.1%.
US recent graduates had an unemployment rate of about 5.6% in the second quarter of 2026 against 4.3% for all workers, and 42% were underemployed.

For internationals the outcomes are worse: post-graduation employment is 44.6% against 62.1% for domestic students, at an average starting salary of $80,785 driven by STEM fields; Duke’s master’s graduates needing a visa had a 71% offer rate at six months against 85% with work rights.

Vietnam’s big graduate programmes recruit through online applications, tests and interviews, and the competition is heavy: Viettel Talent 2026 drew nearly 12,000 applications. English is asked for in the better roles, and employers in a 2018 survey called Vietnamese-owned firms more hierarchical than foreign ones. Graduates back from abroad without local contacts reported little to lean on.
Graduate and management-trainee programmes

No survey ranks the routes in Vietnam; this is first because the large employers found recruit this way, and the competition shows it: Viettel Talent 2026 drew nearly 12,000 applications from 13 countries (about 8,800 to its technical track and nearly 3,000 to its management track), and more than 800 trainees attended its opening on 11 May 2026.

Techcombank Future Gen is a 24-month rotational programme for final-year students and people with under 2 years of experience, in four tracks (Technology, Digital & Data, Business, General Management); the 2025 edition opened for applications in June 2024.

Vietcombank recruits branch staff in waves: in wave III of 2026, regular candidates took a professional exam and an interview, while outstanding graduates of six named universities went to interview only. BIDV’s wave I of 2026 had six customer-relationship-manager groups, two of them for foreign-invested clients in Korean or Chinese.
Internships that turn into offers

Grant Thornton Hanoi’s 2026 internship (audit or tax) took final-year students with an average mark of 7.0 or above for at least 3 months from January to March 2026; the deadline was 17 September 2025. The page does not say how many interns are hired.

Viettel Digital Talent, a technology internship, reports that across the 2021–2025 seasons nearly 1,200 interns were trained and over 400 became Viettel employees while still studying. FPT Software’s fresher programme pays a training allowance for 3 to 6 months with a chance to become full-time.
University job fairs and campus recruiting

HUTECH’s technology exhibition and recruitment day on 7 May 2026 gathered nearly 180 companies offering nearly 7,000 jobs and internships, with students able to apply on the spot. We found no count of how many graduates are hired through fairs.
Job portals and direct application

VietnamWorks (run by Navigos Group), ITviec for IT jobs and CareerViet (whose banner showed 19,681 openings) are the portals read; VietnamWorks takes one CV per application as .doc, .docx or .pdf under 5,120 KB and cannot be re-applied to.

For experienced hires, Vietcetera (2021) describes the three months from Tet to April as the best time to recruit because job-seekers have just received their yearly bonus; Vietcombank’s wave III kept experienced posts open until 31 December 2026 or until the quota was filled.
Referral and networks

Times Higher Education, summarising one researcher’s interviews, says most returning undergraduates who had never worked in Vietnam had “no point of leverage”, while postgraduates on government scholarships already had networks. In the British Council survey of 150 employers, 66% agreed that people who studied abroad know the local market less well.
Recruitment agencies

Adecco Vietnam’s general director, quoted in the British Council report, said clients would love to hire graduates who have spent time overseas for their language skills. We found no count of graduate hires made through agencies.

Programmes recruit from February to June: Viettel opened registration on 12 February 2026 and its trainees started on 11 May; FPT Software’s 2026 fresher post gave a deadline of 3 April (the page also lists 4 May); Vietcombank’s wave III closed on 14 June 2026 for posts needing no experience and BIDV’s wave I on 16 June 2026.

Some windows open much earlier: Grant Thornton Hanoi’s deadline for its January–March 2026 internship was 17 September 2025, and Techcombank’s Future Gen opened in June 2024 for its 2025 edition, through September 2024.
Experienced hiring peaks after Tet (a public holiday from 14 to 22 February 2026), which Vietcetera called a three-month “golden period” until April; its figures are from 2021.

Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track names six universities: National Economics University, Foreign Trade University (Hanoi), Academy of Finance, Banking Academy, Banking University of Ho Chi Minh City and University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City.

For degrees from abroad, 88% of the 150 employers in the British Council survey agreed that studying overseas adds value, and Adecco Vietnam’s director said clients mostly want good English rather than a particular country. The survey dates from 2018.

Vietcombank and BIDV recruit graduates in national waves. The British Council report, citing a 2015 World Bank paper, puts state salaries at about 30% of the median wage and says this may deter overseas graduates from public-sector work; we found no figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hires, so the weight is our reading.

A fresh graduate does not meet the foreign-expert test (a degree plus 2 years of relevant experience, 1 year in technology, digital transformation and finance), and the graduate programmes read do not mention visas. See Visas for the rules. This is our reading.
Grant Thornton Hanoi asks for a recent photo attached to the application; the VietnamWorks pages read do not mention photos. This is our reading.

VietnamWorks’s CV guide ties a second page to substantial experience and suggests trimming to one page when it cannot be filled; Grant Thornton asks for the application and CV in English, under 2MB in total.
VietnamWorks lets each employer mark the cover letter Required, Optional or Not Required; the programme pages read (Viettel, FPT, Grant Thornton, Vietcombank) do not mention one.
None of the programme pages read asks for references with the application. This is our reading.

Grant Thornton asks for the transcript attached to the application, and Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track asks for language and IT certificates. The pages read do not ask for certified or translated copies at application. This is our reading.
None of the programme pages read states a salary or asks for an expectation; FPT’s fresher post lists the training salary as “being updated”. This is our reading.
We found nothing on routine reference checks. A foreign hire needs a criminal-record certificate valid under 6 months, a legalised degree and a medical check for the work permit. See Visas.
Programmes take open online applications in large numbers, yet returning graduates reported having no contacts to lean on, so both apply. This is our reading of the sources.
Viettel’s 2026 intake took applications from 13 countries, but the foreign-worker route needs 2 years of experience and takes 8 to 12 weeks, and the visa-free stay does not allow work. See Visas.

Vietnamese for local firms and the programme pages read; English is asked for in the better graduate roles (FPT TOEIC 700+, Vietcombank IELTS 7.0 on one track) and 77% of foreign companies called it particularly important.

Vietcombank’s regular route in 2026 was two rounds, a professional-knowledge exam then an interview; outstanding graduates skip the exam. Grant Thornton Hanoi uses a technical test, or an IQ test and an English test for those exempt from it, then an interview.

FPT Software contacts only the selected candidates by email after an online application, and trains them for 3 to 6 months; Techcombank says it looks for Ability, Aspiration and Commitment but does not describe its stages. The Viettel pages read do not describe theirs either.
We did not establish the typical time from application to offer, interview dress and punctuality norms, how common video interviews are, or whether the Vietnamese programmes use assessment centres.

A written contract is required except for jobs under one month; it is indefinite-term or fixed-term up to 36 months (renewable once). Probation is up to 60 days for jobs needing a college degree or higher, pay during it must be at least 85% of the normal salary, and no notice is needed to end it.

Notice is 45 days on an indefinite contract, 30 days on a fixed term of 1 to 3 years and 3 working days for seasonal work. After 12 months, severance is generally half a month’s salary per year of service, with final payments within 14 working days.

A thirteenth-month salary is customary but not required by law; the regional minimum wage is VND 3,700,000 to 5,310,000 a month in 2026, the standard week is 48 hours and paid leave is 12 days after 12 months. Average monthly income of employees was VND 9 million in the first half of 2026.

In the 2018 survey, 33% of employers had failed to fill positions because the pay they offered missed candidates’ expectations, and 56% said local graduates ask for less; this points to salary being discussed. We did not establish whether graduates negotiate or how long employers give to decide.

A foreign expert needs a university degree plus 2 years of relevant experience (1 year in science and technology, digital transformation, semiconductors, AI or strategic finance), so a fresh graduate generally does not qualify. The employer must advertise the post for 5 working days and file with DOLISA; the statutory time is about 35 working days, in practice 8 to 12 weeks.

Foreign students currently enrolled with an internship agreement or a job offer from a Vietnamese entity are exempt from the work permit once DOLISA certifies it, at no state fee. The employer must apply for the certificate, so ask early.

Entering visa-free (45 days for citizens of 18 EU countries and the UK) allows visits and interviews but not work; working without the permit risks expulsion and a fine of VND 15 to 25 million. Legalised degrees and a criminal-record certificate under 6 months old are needed. Whether employers will do all this for a new graduate is our reading: the sources do not say.
Portals: VietnamWorks (run by Navigos Group), ITviec for IT jobs (English and Vietnamese) and CareerViet; BIDV applies through its recruitment portal (tuyendung.bidv.com.vn).

Employer programmes: Viettel Talent (Viettel Digital Talent and Viettel Future Changemakers), Techcombank Future Gen, FPT Software’s fresher programme, Vietcombank’s branch waves and Grant Thornton’s internships.

University fairs and services: HUTECH’s technology and recruitment day (7 May 2026) in Ho Chi Minh City; for others, follow your university’s career or student office, since fairs are announced a few weeks ahead.
Recruitment firms such as Adecco Vietnam work with clients that value overseas-educated graduates.
Applying too late: Grant Thornton Hanoi’s January internship closed on 17 September, Viettel opened registration on 12 February and Vietcombank and BIDV closed in mid-June 2026.
Treating English as a formality: FPT asks for TOEIC 700+ equivalent, Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track for IELTS 7.0 or equivalent, and Grant Thornton adds an English test.
Starting work on a visa-free stay: it does not allow work, and working without the permit risks expulsion and a fine of VND 15 to 25 million.
Overpricing yourself after a degree abroad: 33% of the 150 employers surveyed in 2018 had failed to fill a post over salary expectations.
Re-applying or sending a second CV on VietnamWorks: it takes one CV per application and does not let you change it or re-apply to the same job.
Counting on a thirteenth-month salary or Tet bonus: neither is required by law, so look for it in the contract.
Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track requires IELTS 7.0, TOEIC 785, TOEFL 550 or CEFR C1 and an office-IT certificate; BIDV has FDI-client tracks in Korean and Chinese.
The British Council report says English is particularly in demand in financial services.
Grant Thornton Hanoi asks for fluent English in reading, writing, speaking and listening, takes the application and CV in English, and sets an English test for those exempt from its technical test.
FPT Software’s fresher post asks for good reading and communication English, equivalent to TOEIC 700+; ITviec offers its pages in English and Vietnamese.

In the 2018 British Council survey, 77% of foreign companies and 76% of conglomerates said English skills were particularly important, and 87% of employers agreed that jobseekers lack language skills; Vietnamese is the language of local firms.

Youth (15–24) unemployment was 8.86% in the first quarter of 2026 against 2.23% for all working-age people in the second quarter; it was 8.6% for 2025 and 9.04% in the fourth quarter. About 1.4 million young people, 10.2% of the youth population, were neither working nor in education or training. We found no graduate-specific figure or return-offer rate for Vietnam.

VnEconomy (August 2026) reports that around 70% of university graduates still need retraining after entering the workforce, and that employers value communication, teamwork and adaptability; the 2018 British Council report says graduate unemployment and underemployment are high because the education system struggles to meet employers’ needs.

DH student visa and residence card
A university authorised to take foreign students requests a DH entry visa, then a temporary residence card for the length of the course.
International students may not work at all, not even part time; private English lessons count, and lead to expulsion and a three-to-five-year ban.
Residence card
$145 up to 2 years, $155 up to 5
Internship with a work-permit exemption

Enrolled students with a three-way internship agreement are exempt from the work permit, but the host must obtain the exemption certificate and you need a DH visa. Graduates cannot intern: anything they do counts as ordinary work.
After graduating
There is no job-search visa: when the student card expires you must leave, unless a work permit or exemption is approved first, which a graduate without two years of experience rarely gets.
Work permit and LĐ2 residence card

The employer advertises the job locally for five working days, then files the work permit with the provincial labour department; you enter on an LĐ2 visa, take a medical at an accredited Vietnamese hospital and get a two-year residence card. Contracts last two years at most.
Experts need a degree and two years of experience, one year in technology, digital, semiconductors, AI or finance.
$145 for 2 years
Research visits and PhDs

Thesis research with a Vietnamese university uses a DH visa; researchers working with Vietnamese institutions without enrolling get an LV2 visa. Fieldwork, sampling or interviews need prior government clearance.
Scholarships are free of income tax, but universities cannot pay foreign PhD students a salary on a DH visa.
Working holiday
Vietnam has working-holiday agreements only with Australia and New Zealand; “teach and travel” offers on a tourist visa are illegal work.
Visa-free visit or e-visa

British citizens and those of 18 EU countries, Italy, Germany, France and Spain among them, enter visa-free for 45 days, not extendable. Austria, Greece, Portugal, Ireland, the Baltic states, Malta and Cyprus need an e-visa of up to 90 days.
E-visa
$25 single entry, $50 multiple

About two months ahead, have your degree, a foreign criminal record under 6 months old and work references legalised: since 11 September 2026 an apostille is enough for Italian documents, while some countries that objected still need consular legalisation.
On the e-visa, the order of your names must match the machine-readable line of your passport exactly, or the airline may refuse to board you.

Whoever houses you must register your temporary residence within 24 hours of arrival; otherwise you face fines of VND 3 to 5 million, and without the registration slip you cannot get the residence card.
A two-year temporary residence card for work (LĐ2) costs USD 145.
Register your employee tax code within 10 working days and join compulsory social and health insurance: 9.5% from you, 20.5% from the company.
Workers need a health check at an accredited Vietnamese hospital, about VND 1,500,000, for a certificate stating that they are fit for work.

Banks may not open accounts for tourist or e-visa holders. Professionals need a passport, a residence card valid at least 12 months, a work contract, a tax code and the residence slip, and must give biometrics in person; accounts freeze the day the card expires.
Whoever houses you must register you with the police within 24 hours; without it you cannot get a residence card.
Working before the work permit is issued means expulsion and a fine of up to 25 million VND.
Names on the e-visa must match the passport’s machine-readable line exactly, or airlines refuse boarding.
Banks cannot open accounts for tourists or e-visa holders, and need face biometrics in person.
A spouse’s family residence card gives no right to work.
Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention on 11 September 2026; provincial offices accept Italian apostilles unevenly.
Medical certificates from Italy are in practice rejected for the work permit.
Whether a visa-free visitor can switch to a work visa inside Vietnam is handled inconsistently.
